verses.37:16: "Now you, son of man, take for yourself one stick and write on it, 'For Judah and for the sons of Israel, his companions'; then take one stick and write on it, 'For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all the house of Israel, his companions.'
verses.37:17: And join them together, one to another, for yourself into one stick, so that they become one in your hand.
verses.37:18: And when the sons of your people speak to you, saying, 'Will you not tell us what these mean to you?'
verses.37:19: speak to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I am about to take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel, his companions, and I will place them with it, with the stick of Judah, and make them into one stick, and they will be one in My hand.'
verses.37:20: And the sticks on which you write will be in your hand before their eyes.
verses.37:21: And speak to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I am about to take the sons of Israel from among the nations where they have gone, and I will gather them from every side and bring them to their own soil.
verses.37:22: And I will make them into one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel; and one king will be king over all of them; and they will no longer be two nations, and they will no longer be divided into two kingdoms ever again.
verses.37:23: And they will no longer defile themselves with their idols, or with their detestable things, or with any of their transgressions; but I will deliver them from all their dwelling places in which they have sinned, and I will cleanse them. And they will be a people to Me, and I will be God to them.
verses.37:24: And My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd for all of them; and they will walk in My ordinances, and they will keep My statutes and do them.
verses.37:25: And they will dwell on the land that I gave to My servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt; and they will dwell upon it—they and their sons and the sons of their sons—forever, and David My servant will be their prince forever.
verses.37:26: And I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant with them. And I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set My sanctuary in their midst forever.
verses.37:27: And My dwelling place will be over them; and I will be God to them, and they will be a people to Me.
verses.37:28: And the nations will know that I am the LORD who sanctifies Israel, when My sanctuary is in their midst forever.'"
verses.38:1: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.38:2: "Son of man, direct your face toward Gog, of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him,
verses.38:3: and say, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
verses.38:4: I will turn you around and put hooks into your jaws, and I will bring you out along with all your army—horses and horsemen, all of them clothed in splendor, a vast company with large shields and small shields, all of them wielding swords.
verses.38:5: With them are Persia, Cush, and Put, every one with shield and helmet.
verses.38:6: Gomer and all its troops, the house of Togarmah of the far reaches of the north and all its troops—many peoples are with you.
verses.38:7: Be ready and prepare yourself, you and all your company assembled around you, and serve as a guard for them.
verses.38:8: After many days you will be summoned; in the latter years you will enter a land brought back from the sword, gathered from many peoples, upon the mountains of Israel, which had been a continual ruin; yet it was brought out from the peoples, and all of them dwell securely.
verses.38:9: You will go up; like a storm you will come; you will be like a cloud to cover the land, you and all your troops, and many peoples with you.
verses.38:10: This is what the Lord GOD says: It will happen on that day that thoughts will rise in your heart, and you will devise an evil scheme,
verses.38:11: and you will say, "I will go up against a land of open villages; I will come upon those who are at rest, dwelling securely—all of them dwelling without a wall, and having neither bar nor gates,"
verses.38:12: to capture spoil and to seize plunder, to turn your hand against ruins now inhabited and against a people gathered from the nations, acquiring livestock and possessions, who dwell at the center of the earth.
verses.38:13: Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish and all its young lions will say to you, "Have you come to capture spoil? Have you assembled your company to seize plunder, to carry off silver and gold, to take livestock and possessions, to capture great spoil?"'
verses.38:14: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and tell Gog, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: In that day, when My people Israel dwell securely, will you not know?
verses.38:15: You will come from your place, from the far reaches of the north—you and many peoples with you, every one riding on horses, a great company and a vast army.
verses.38:16: You will go up against My people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. It will happen in the latter days that I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I show Myself holy through you before their eyes, Gog.
verses.38:17: This is what the Lord GOD says: Are you the one about whom I spoke in earlier days by My servants, the prophets of Israel, who prophesied for years in those days that I would bring you against them?
verses.38:18: It will happen on that day, the day when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, that My fury will rise in My anger.
verses.38:19: And in My jealousy, in the fire of My wrath, I have spoken: Surely on that day there will be a great earthquake upon the land of Israel.
verses.38:20: The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the beasts of the field, every creeping thing that creeps on the ground, and every human being on the face of the ground will quake at My presence; the mountains will be torn down, the cliffs will fall, and every wall will fall to the earth.
verses.38:21: I will summon a sword against him throughout all My mountains, declares the Lord GOD; the sword of each man will be against his brother.
verses.38:22: I will enter into judgment with him by pestilence and bloodshed, and I will rain down torrential rain and hailstones, fire and sulfur, upon him and upon his troops and upon the many peoples who are with him.
verses.38:23: And I will show Myself great and show Myself holy, and I will make Myself known before the eyes of many nations; then they will know that I am the LORD.'"
verses.39:1: "And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
verses.39:2: I will turn you around and lead you forward, and I will bring you up from the far reaches of the north and bring you onto the mountains of Israel.
verses.39:3: I will knock your bow out of your left hand and cause your arrows to fall from your right hand.
verses.39:4: On the mountains of Israel you will fall, you and all your troops and the peoples who are with you; I will give you as food to birds of prey of every wing and to the beasts of the field.
verses.39:5: Upon the open field you will fall, for I Myself have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.39:6: And I will send fire into Magog and among those who live securely in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the LORD.
verses.39:7: My holy name I will make known in the midst of My people Israel, and I will no longer let My holy name be profaned; and the nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
verses.39:8: Look, it is coming and it will be brought about, declares the Lord GOD; that is the day of which I have spoken.
verses.39:9: Then the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go out and set fire to and burn the weapons—small shields and large shields, bows and arrows, hand clubs and spears—and they will make fires with them for seven years.
verses.39:10: They will not carry wood from the field nor cut any from the forests, for they will make fires with the weapons; and they will despoil those who despoiled them and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.39:11: It will happen on that day that I will give Gog a burial place there in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the sea, and it will block the travelers; there they will bury Gog and all his multitude, and they will call it the Valley of Hamon-gog.
verses.39:12: And the house of Israel will bury them for seven months so that they may cleanse the land.
verses.39:13: All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day I am glorified, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.39:14: They will set apart men on continual duty to pass through the land, and with those passing through, men burying those left on the face of the land to cleanse it; at the end of seven months they will make a search.
verses.39:15: As those passing through go through the land, whenever anyone sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it until the buriers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
verses.39:16: And the name of a city will also be Hamonah. Thus they will cleanse the land.'
verses.39:17: And you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: Speak to the birds of every wing and to every beast of the field, 'Assemble and come; gather from all around to My sacrifice that I am sacrificing for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel, and you will eat flesh and drink blood.
verses.39:18: You will eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of the princes of the earth—rams, lambs, and male goats, bulls, all of them fattened animals of Bashan.
verses.39:19: You will eat fat to fullness and drink blood to drunkenness, from My sacrifice that I have sacrificed for you.
verses.39:20: You will be filled at My table with horses and charioteers, with mighty men and every man of war, declares the Lord GOD.'
verses.39:21: I will place My glory among the nations, and all the nations will see My judgment that I have carried out and My hand that I have put upon them.
verses.39:22: Then the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God from that day onward.
verses.39:23: And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile on account of their iniquity, because they acted unfaithfully against Me; so I hid My face from them and delivered them into the hand of their adversaries, and all of them fell by the sword.
verses.39:24: I dealt with them according to their impurity and their transgressions, and I hid My face from them.
verses.39:25: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on the entire house of Israel, and I will be jealous for My holy name.
verses.39:26: They will bear their disgrace and all the unfaithfulness that they committed against Me, when they dwell securely on their land with no one to make them afraid.
verses.39:27: When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, I will show Myself holy through them before the eyes of the many nations.
verses.39:28: Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, because I sent them into exile among the nations and then gathered them to their land, and I will not leave any of them there anymore.
verses.39:29: And I will never again hide My face from them, since I have poured out My Spirit upon the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD."
verses.40:1: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down, on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He brought me there.
verses.40:2: In visions of God He brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain, and on it was something like the structure of a city to the south.
verses.40:3: He brought me there, and look, there was a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze, with a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand, and he was standing in the gate.
verses.40:4: The man spoke to me, "Son of man, see with your eyes and hear with your ears, and set your heart on everything that I am showing you, for you have been brought here in order that I might show it to you. Declare everything that you see to the house of Israel."
verses.40:5: And look, there was a wall outside the house all around, and in the man's hand was the measuring reed, six cubits, each a cubit and a handbreadth. He measured the width of the structure, one reed, and the height, one reed.
verses.40:6: Then he came to a gate that faced toward the east and went up its steps. He measured the threshold of the gate, one reed in width, and the other threshold, one reed in width.
verses.40:7: Each guardroom was one reed in length and one reed in width, and between the guardrooms was five cubits; and the threshold of the gate beside the vestibule of the gate toward the house was one reed.
verses.40:8: He measured the vestibule of the gate toward the house, one reed.
verses.40:9: Then he measured the vestibule of the gate, eight cubits, and its jambs, two cubits; and the vestibule of the gate was toward the house.
verses.40:10: The guardrooms of the gate toward the east were three on this side and three on that side; the three of them had one measurement, and the jambs on this side and on that side had one measurement.
verses.40:11: He measured the width of the entrance of the gate, ten cubits, and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits.
verses.40:12: There was a border in front of the guardrooms of one cubit, and a border of one cubit on the other side; and each guardroom was six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.
verses.40:13: He measured the gate from the roof of one guardroom to the opposite roof, a width of twenty-five cubits, entrance opposite entrance.
verses.40:14: He also made the jambs sixty cubits, and up to the jamb of the court was the gate all around.
verses.40:15: From the front of the entrance gate to the front of the inner vestibule of the gate was fifty cubits.
verses.40:16: There were narrowed windows for the guardrooms and for their jambs inside the gate all around, and likewise for the vestibules; windows were all around on the inside, and on each jamb were palm ornaments.
verses.40:17: Then he brought me into the outer court, and look, there were chambers and a pavement made for the court all around; thirty chambers were along the pavement.
verses.40:18: The pavement was along the side of the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates; this was the lower pavement.
verses.40:19: Then he measured the width from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court on the outside, one hundred cubits, on the east and on the north.
verses.40:20: As for the gate of the outer court that faced toward the north, he measured its length and its width.
verses.40:21: Its guardrooms were three on this side and three on that side, and its jambs and its vestibule were according to the measurement of the first gate: its length was fifty cubits, and the width was twenty-five cubits.
verses.40:22: Its windows, its vestibule, and its palm ornaments were according to the measurement of the gate that faced toward the east; they would go up to it by seven steps, and its vestibule was in front of them.
verses.40:23: There was a gate to the inner court opposite the gate on the north and on the east, and he measured from gate to gate, one hundred cubits.
verses.40:24: Then he led me toward the south, and look, there was a gate toward the south; and he measured its jambs and its vestibule according to these measurements.
verses.40:25: It and its vestibule had windows all around, like these windows; the length was fifty cubits, and the width was twenty-five cubits.
verses.40:26: There were seven steps going up to it, and its vestibule was in front of them; and it had palm ornaments, one on this side and one on that side, on its jambs.
verses.40:27: There was a gate to the inner court toward the south, and he measured from gate to gate toward the south, one hundred cubits.
verses.40:28: Then he brought me into the inner court by the south gate, and he measured the south gate according to these measurements.
verses.40:29: Its guardrooms, its jambs, and its vestibule were according to these measurements. It and its vestibule had windows all around; the length was fifty cubits, and the width was twenty-five cubits.
verses.40:31: Its vestibule was toward the outer court, palm ornaments were on its jambs, and its ascent had eight steps.
verses.40:32: Then he brought me into the inner court toward the east, and he measured the gate according to these measurements.
verses.40:33: Its guardrooms, its jambs, and its vestibule were according to these measurements. It and its vestibule had windows all around; the length was fifty cubits, and the width was twenty-five cubits.
verses.40:34: Its vestibule was toward the outer court, palm ornaments were on its jambs on this side and on that side, and its ascent had eight steps.
verses.40:35: Then he brought me to the north gate, and he measured according to these measurements:
verses.40:36: its guardrooms, its jambs, and its vestibule; and it had windows all around. The length was fifty cubits, and the width was twenty-five cubits.
verses.40:37: Its jambs were toward the outer court, palm ornaments were on its jambs on this side and on that side, and its ascent had eight steps.
verses.40:38: There was a chamber with its entrance by the jambs of the gates; there they would rinse the burnt offering.
verses.40:39: In the vestibule of the gate were two tables on this side and two tables on that side, on which to slaughter the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
verses.40:40: On the outer side, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gate, were two tables, and on the other side, belonging to the vestibule of the gate, were two tables.
verses.40:41: Four tables were on this side and four tables on that side, at the side of the gate, eight tables on which they would slaughter.
verses.40:42: There were also four tables of hewn stone for the burnt offering, one and a half cubits in length, one and a half cubits in width, and one cubit in height; on them they would lay the instruments with which they would slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice.
verses.40:43: And double hooks, one handbreadth long, were fastened inside all around; and on the tables was the flesh of the offering.
verses.40:44: Outside the inner gate were chambers for singers in the inner court, at the side of the north gate, facing toward the south; one was at the side of the east gate, facing toward the north.
verses.40:45: He spoke to me, "This chamber, which faces toward the south, is for the priests who keep the charge of the house;
verses.40:46: and the chamber that faces toward the north is for the priests who keep the charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who from among the sons of Levi draw near to the LORD to minister to Him."
verses.40:47: He measured the court: a length of one hundred cubits and a width of one hundred cubits, square; and the altar was in front of the house.
verses.40:48: Then he brought me to the vestibule of the house and measured the jamb of the vestibule, five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side; and the width of the gate was three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.
verses.40:49: The length of the vestibule was twenty cubits, and the width was eleven cubits; and there were steps by which they would go up to it, and pillars beside the jambs, one on this side and one on that side.
verses.41:1: Then he brought me to the temple hall and measured the jambs, six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other side, the width of the tent.
verses.41:2: The width of the entrance was ten cubits, and the side walls of the entrance were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other side. He also measured its length, forty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits.
verses.41:3: Then he went inside and measured the jamb of the entrance, two cubits, and the entrance, six cubits, and the width of the entrance, seven cubits.
verses.41:4: He measured its length, twenty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits, before the temple hall; and he said to me, "This is the Most Holy Place."
verses.41:5: Then he measured the wall of the house, six cubits, and the width of the side room, four cubits, all around the house on every side.
verses.41:6: Now the side rooms were side room over side room, thirty-three times; and they extended into the wall that belonged to the house for the side rooms all around so as to be fastened, yet they were not fastened in the wall of the house.
verses.41:7: It broadened and wound around higher and higher for the side rooms, for the surrounding structure of the house went higher and higher all around the house; therefore the house had greater width upward, and so one went up from the lowest story to the highest by way of the middle.
verses.41:8: And I saw an elevation for the house all around; the foundations of the side rooms were a full reed, six cubits to the joint.
verses.41:9: The width of the wall belonging to the side room on the outside was five cubits, and the open space was beside the side-room structure belonging to the house.
verses.41:10: And between the chambers was a width of twenty cubits around the house on every side.
verses.41:11: The entrance of the side room was toward the open space, one entrance toward the north and one entrance toward the south; and the width of the area of the open space was five cubits all around.
verses.41:12: Now the building that was in front of the separated space on the side toward the west was seventy cubits wide; the wall of the building was five cubits wide all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
verses.41:13: Then he measured the house, a hundred cubits in length; and the separated space and the building and its walls were a hundred cubits in length.
verses.41:14: And the width of the front of the house and of the separated space toward the east was a hundred cubits.
verses.41:15: He measured the length of the building in front of the separated space that was behind it, together with its galleries on one side and on the other side, a hundred cubits. Now the inner temple hall and the porticoes of the court,
verses.41:16: the thresholds, the narrowed windows, and the galleries around all three of them, opposite the threshold, were paneled with wood all around, from the floor up to the windows—and the windows were covered—
verses.41:17: to the space above the entrance, and even to the inner house and on the outside, and on the entire wall all around, inside and outside, by measurements.
verses.41:18: It was made with cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between cherub and cherub, and each cherub had two faces.
verses.41:19: The face of a man was toward the palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion was toward the palm tree on the other side; it was made on the entire house all around.
verses.41:20: From the floor up to above the entrance, the cherubim and the palm trees were made, and on the wall of the temple hall.
verses.41:21: The temple hall had a square doorpost, and as for the front of the sanctuary, the appearance was the same.
verses.41:22: The altar was of wood, three cubits high, and its length was two cubits; its corners belonged to it, and its length and its walls were of wood. And he spoke to me, "This is the table that is before the LORD."
verses.41:23: The temple hall and the sanctuary each had two doors.
verses.41:24: And the doors had two leaves each, two swinging leaves: two for one door and two leaves for the other.
verses.41:25: And on them, on the doors of the temple hall, cherubim and palm trees were made, just as they were made on the walls; and there was a wooden overhang in front of the portico on the outside.
verses.41:26: And there were narrowed windows and palm trees on one side and on the other side, on the side walls of the portico, as well as the side rooms of the house and the overhangs.
verses.42:1: Then he led me out to the outer court by the way toward the north, and he brought me to the chamber that was opposite the separated space and opposite the building toward the north.
verses.42:2: Facing the length of a hundred cubits was the north entrance, and the width was fifty cubits.
verses.42:3: Opposite the twenty cubits belonging to the inner court and opposite the pavement belonging to the outer court was gallery facing gallery in three stories.
verses.42:4: In front of the chambers was a walkway ten cubits wide toward the inside, a passage of one cubit, and their entrances were toward the north.
verses.42:5: Now the upper chambers were shorter, for galleries took space away from them more than from the lower and the middle ones of the building.
verses.42:6: For they were in three stories and did not have pillars like the pillars of the courts; therefore the upper ones were set back more than the lower and the middle ones from the ground.
verses.42:7: And there was a wall outside, parallel to the chambers, toward the outer court in front of the chambers; its length was fifty cubits.
verses.42:8: For the length of the chambers belonging to the outer court was fifty cubits, and look, those facing the temple hall were a hundred cubits.
verses.42:9: And below these chambers was the entryway from the east, as one enters them from the outer court.
verses.42:10: In the width of the wall of the court toward the east, in front of the separated space and in front of the building, there were chambers.
verses.42:11: And there was a passage in front of them, like the appearance of the chambers that were toward the north, matching both their length and their width, and all their exits, according to their arrangements and their entrances.
verses.42:12: And corresponding to the entrances of the chambers that were toward the south was an entrance at the head of the passage, the passage in front of the matching wall toward the east, as one enters them.
verses.42:13: Then he said to me, "The north chambers and the south chambers that are in front of the separated space are the holy chambers, where the priests who are near to the LORD shall eat the most holy things. There they shall place the most holy things: the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, for the place is holy.
verses.42:14: When the priests enter, they shall not go out from the sanctuary into the outer court, but there they shall place their garments in which they minister, for they are holy; and they shall put on other garments, and then draw near to what belongs to the people."
verses.42:15: Now when he had finished the measurements of the inner house, he led me out by way of the gate whose front was toward the east, and he measured it all around.
verses.42:16: He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around.
verses.42:17: He measured the north side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around.
verses.42:18: He measured the south side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.42:19: He turned to the west side and measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.42:20: He measured it on the four sides; it had a wall all around, five hundred in length and five hundred in width, to separate between the holy and the common.
verses.43:1: And he led me to the gate, a gate that faces toward the east.
verses.43:2: And look, the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the way of the east; His voice was like the sound of many waters, and the earth grew bright from His glory.
verses.43:3: And it was like the appearance of the vision that I saw, like the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city, and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the Chebar River; and I fell on my face.
verses.43:4: And the glory of the LORD came into the house by way of the gate whose front is toward the east.
verses.43:5: Then a spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner courtyard; and look, the glory of the LORD filled the house.
verses.43:6: And I heard someone speaking to me from out of the house, while a man was standing next to me.
verses.43:7: And He said to me, "Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place of the soles of My feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel forever. And the house of Israel will no longer defile My holy name—neither they nor their kings—by their prostitution and by the corpses of their kings at their high places.
verses.43:8: When they set their threshold beside My threshold and their doorpost next to My doorpost, with the wall between Me and them, they defiled My holy name by their abominations that they committed, so I consumed them in My anger.
verses.43:9: Now let them put their prostitution and the corpses of their kings far away from Me, and I will dwell in their midst forever.
verses.43:10: As for you, son of man, describe the house to the house of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities; and let them measure the pattern.
verses.43:11: And if they are ashamed of all that they have done, make known to them the design of the house, its arrangement, its exits, its entrances, all its designs, all its statutes, all its designs, and all its laws, and write it before their eyes, so that they may keep its entire design and all its statutes and do them.
verses.43:12: This is the law of the house: on the top of the mountain, its entire territory all around shall be most holy. Look, this is the law of the house."
verses.43:13: And these are the measurements of the altar in cubits—a cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth: the base is one cubit, and it is one cubit wide, and its border along its edge all around is one span; and this is the pedestal of the altar.
verses.43:14: And from the base on the ground to the lower ledge is two cubits, with a width of one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge is four cubits, with a width of one cubit.
verses.43:15: And the altar hearth is four cubits, and from the altar hearth upward are four horns.
verses.43:16: And the altar hearth is twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.
verses.43:17: And the ledge is fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide on its four sides, and the border around it is half a cubit, and its base is one cubit all around; and its steps face east.
verses.43:18: And He said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: These are the statutes of the altar on the day it is made, to offer up a burnt offering on it and to splash blood on it.
verses.43:19: You shall give to the Levitical priests who are from the seed of Zadok, who draw near to Me, declares the Lord GOD, to minister to Me, a bull from the herd for a sin offering.
verses.43:20: And you shall take some of its blood and put it on its four horns, and on the four corners of the ledge, and on the border all around; thus you shall purify it and make atonement for it.
verses.43:21: You shall also take the bull for the sin offering, and it shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
verses.43:22: And on the second day you shall present a male goat without blemish for a sin offering, and they shall purify the altar just as they purified it with the bull.
verses.43:23: When you have finished purifying it, you shall present a bull from the herd without blemish and a ram from the flock without blemish.
verses.43:24: You shall present them before the LORD, and the priests shall cast salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.43:25: For seven days you shall offer a male goat for a sin offering each day; and they shall offer a bull from the herd and a ram from the flock, without blemish.
verses.43:26: For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and so consecrate it.
verses.43:27: When they have completed the days, it shall be that on the eighth day and onward, the priests shall offer on the altar your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, and I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD."
verses.44:1: Then he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faces east, and it was shut.
verses.44:2: And the LORD said to me, "This gate shall remain shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it; therefore it shall remain shut.
verses.44:3: As for the prince, since he is the prince, he may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD; he shall enter by way of the porch of the gate and go out by that same way."
verses.44:4: Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house; and I saw, and look, the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD, and I fell on my face.
verses.44:5: And the LORD said to me, "Son of man, pay careful attention, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I am speaking to you concerning all the statutes of the house of the LORD and all its laws; and pay careful attention to the entrance of the house, along with all the exits of the sanctuary.
verses.44:6: And you shall say to the rebellious ones, to the house of Israel, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel,
verses.44:7: in bringing in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My sanctuary to profane My house, when you present My food, fat and blood; and they broke My covenant in addition to all your abominations.
verses.44:8: And you have not kept the charge of My holy things, but you appointed them as keepers of My charge in My sanctuary for yourselves.
verses.44:9: This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter My sanctuary, not any foreigner who is in the midst of the sons of Israel.
verses.44:10: Rather, the Levites who went far away from Me when Israel went astray, who went astray from Me after their idols, they shall bear their iniquity.
verses.44:11: They shall be ministers in My sanctuary, having oversight at the gates of the house and ministering to the house; they shall slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to minister to them.
verses.44:12: Because they ministered to them before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I have lifted up My hand against them, declares the Lord GOD, and they shall bear their iniquity.
verses.44:13: And they shall not approach Me to serve as priests to Me, nor approach any of My holy things, to the most holy things; but they shall bear their disgrace and their abominations that they have committed.
verses.44:14: Yet I will appoint them as keepers of the charge of the house, for all its service and for everything that is to be done in it.
verses.44:15: But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of My sanctuary when the sons of Israel went astray from Me, they shall draw near to Me to minister to Me, and they shall stand before Me to present to Me fat and blood, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.44:16: They shall enter My sanctuary, and they shall draw near to My table to minister to Me, and they shall keep My charge.
verses.44:17: And it shall be that when they enter the gates of the inner courtyard, they shall wear linen garments; and no wool shall come upon them while they minister at the gates of the inner courtyard and inside the house.
verses.44:18: Linen turbans shall be on their heads, and linen undergarments shall be on their loins; they shall not bind themselves with anything that causes sweat.
verses.44:19: And when they go out to the outer courtyard, to the outer courtyard to the people, they shall take off their garments in which they minister and lay them in the holy chambers; and they shall put on other garments, so that they will not make the people holy with their garments.
verses.44:20: And they shall not shave their heads, nor let their hair grow long; they shall certainly trim the hair on their heads.
verses.44:21: And no priest shall drink wine when entering the inner courtyard.
verses.44:22: And they shall not take a widow or a divorced woman for themselves as wives, but only virgins from the seed of the house of Israel, or they may take a widow who is the widow of a priest.
verses.44:23: And they shall teach My people to discern between the holy and the common, and make them know the distinction between the unclean and the clean.
verses.44:24: And in a dispute they shall stand for judgment; by My judgments they shall judge it. And they shall keep My laws and My statutes in all My appointed festivals, and they shall keep My Sabbaths holy.
verses.44:25: And none of them shall come near a dead person to become defiled; however, for a father or mother, for a son or daughter, for a brother, or for a sister who has had no husband, they may defile themselves.
verses.44:26: And after his cleansing, they shall count seven days for him.
verses.44:27: And on the day he enters the holy place, into the inner courtyard, to minister in the holy place, he shall present his sin offering, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.44:28: And this shall be an inheritance for them: I am their inheritance; and you shall not give them a possession in Israel: I am their possession.
verses.44:29: The grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering—they shall eat them; and every devoted thing in Israel shall belong to them.
verses.44:30: And the first of all the firstfruits of every kind, and every contribution of every kind from all your contributions, shall belong to the priests; you shall also give the first of your dough to the priest, to cause a blessing to rest on your house.
verses.44:31: The priests shall not eat anything that dies of itself or is torn, whether of bird or of animal.'"
verses.45:1: "And when you divide the land by lot for an inheritance, you shall set apart a contribution to the LORD, a holy portion of the land: its length shall be twenty-five thousand, and its width ten thousand; it shall be holy throughout its entire border all around.
verses.45:2: Of this there shall be for the sanctuary five hundred by five hundred, square all around, with fifty cubits of open space for it all around.
verses.45:3: From this measured area you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand, and within it shall be the sanctuary, the most holy place.
verses.45:4: It shall be a holy portion of the land for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who draw near to minister to the LORD; it shall serve them as a place for houses and as a sacred site for the sanctuary.
verses.45:5: And twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width shall belong to the Levites, the ministers of the house, for themselves as a possession, twenty chambers.
verses.45:6: As the possession of the city you shall assign five thousand in width and twenty-five thousand in length, alongside the sacred contribution; it shall belong to the entire house of Israel.
verses.45:7: And the prince shall have land on this side and on that side of the sacred contribution and of the possession of the city, fronting the sacred contribution and fronting the possession of the city, from the western side westward and from the eastern side eastward, with a length corresponding to one of the portions, from the western border to the eastern border.
verses.45:8: This land shall be his as a possession in Israel; and My princes shall no longer oppress My people, but they shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes."
verses.45:9: This is what the Lord GOD says: "Enough for you, princes of Israel! Put away violence and devastation, and practice justice and righteousness. Lift your evictions off My people," declares the Lord GOD.
verses.45:10: "You shall have honest scales, an honest ephah, and an honest bath.
verses.45:11: The ephah and the bath shall have a single standard measure, so that the bath holds a tenth of a homer and the ephah a tenth of a homer; its standard measure shall be regulated by the homer.
verses.45:12: The shekel shall be twenty gerahs; twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels shall be your mina.
verses.45:13: This is the contribution that you shall set apart: a sixth of an ephah from a homer of wheat, and you shall give a sixth of an ephah from a homer of barley.
verses.45:14: And the prescribed portion of oil, by the bath of oil, shall be a tenth of a bath from each kor; ten baths are a homer, for ten baths make a homer.
verses.45:15: And one sheep from the flock out of every two hundred, from the watered pastures of Israel, shall be for a grain offering, a burnt offering, and peace offerings, to make atonement for them," declares the Lord GOD.
verses.45:16: "All the people of the land shall share in this contribution for the prince in Israel.
verses.45:17: And the prince shall be responsible for the burnt offerings, the grain offering, and the drink offering at the festivals, on the new moons, and on the Sabbaths, at all the appointed times of the house of Israel; he himself shall prepare the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement on behalf of the house of Israel."
verses.45:18: This is what the Lord GOD says: "In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary.
verses.45:19: The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorpost of the house, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the post of the gate of the inner court.
verses.45:20: You shall do the same on the seventh day of the month on account of anyone who errs unintentionally or through ignorance; thus you shall make atonement for the house.
verses.45:21: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a festival of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.
verses.45:22: On that day the prince shall prepare for himself and for all the people of the land a bull as a sin offering.
verses.45:23: During the seven days of the festival he shall prepare as a burnt offering to the LORD seven bulls and seven rams without blemish daily for the seven days, and a male goat daily as a sin offering.
verses.45:24: And he shall prepare as a grain offering an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.45:25: In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, during the festival, he shall prepare the same for the seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and oil."
verses.46:1: This is what the Lord GOD says: "The gate of the inner court that faces east shall remain shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.
verses.46:2: The prince shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate from outside and stand beside the post of the gate. Then the priests shall offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall bow down in worship at the threshold of the gate and go out; yet the gate shall not be shut until evening.
verses.46:3: The people of the land shall also bow down in worship at the entrance of that gate before the LORD on the Sabbaths and on the new moons.
verses.46:4: The burnt offering that the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish,
verses.46:5: with a grain offering of an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs a grain offering of whatever his hand gives, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.46:6: On the day of the new moon it shall be a young bull without blemish, and six lambs and a ram; they shall be without blemish.
verses.46:7: He shall prepare as a grain offering an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs as much as his hand can afford, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.46:8: When the prince enters, he shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate, and by the same way he shall go out.
verses.46:9: But when the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed times, whoever enters by way of the north gate to bow down in worship shall go out by way of the south gate, and whoever enters by way of the south gate shall go out by way of the north gate; he shall not return by way of the gate through which he entered, but shall go out straight ahead.
verses.46:10: As for the prince, he shall be in their midst: when they enter, he shall enter, and when they go out, they shall go out.
verses.46:11: At the festivals and at the appointed times, the grain offering shall be an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, and for the lambs whatever his hand gives, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.46:12: When the prince prepares a freewill offering, either a burnt offering or peace offerings as a freewill offering to the LORD, the gate that faces east shall be opened for him, and he shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and the gate shall be shut after he goes out.
verses.46:13: You shall also prepare a year-old lamb without blemish as a burnt offering daily to the LORD; morning by morning you shall prepare it.
verses.46:14: And with it you shall prepare a grain offering morning by morning: a sixth of an ephah, and a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour, a grain offering to the LORD by perpetual statutes continually.
verses.46:15: They shall prepare the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil morning by morning as a continual burnt offering."
verses.46:16: This is what the Lord GOD says: "If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance; it shall belong to his sons; it is their possession by inheritance.
verses.46:17: But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of liberty, and then it shall return to the prince; but as for his inheritance, it shall belong to his sons; it shall be theirs.
verses.46:18: The prince shall not take any of the people's inheritance, oppressing them out of their possession; from his own possession he shall give an inheritance to his sons, so that My people will not be scattered, each man from his possession."
verses.46:19: Then he brought me through the entrance that was at the side of the gate into the holy chambers for the priests, which faced north; and look, a place was there at the extreme rear toward the west.
verses.46:20: And he said to me, "This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so as not to bring them out into the outer court and consecrate the people."
verses.46:21: Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me over to the four corners of the court; and look, in every corner of the court there was a court.
verses.46:22: In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, forty in length and thirty in width; these four corner courts had one measurement.
verses.46:23: There was a masonry row all around inside them, around all four of them, and boiling hearths were built beneath the rows all around.
verses.46:24: And he said to me, "These are the cooking houses where the ministers of the house shall boil the sacrifice of the people."
verses.47:1: Then he brought me back to the entrance of the house, and look, water was coming out from beneath the threshold of the house toward the east, for the front of the house faced east; and the water was flowing down from beneath the right side of the house, south of the altar.
verses.47:2: He brought me out by way of the north gate and led me around on the outside to the outer gate that faces east; and look, water was trickling out from the right side.
verses.47:3: As the man went out eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured a thousand cubits and led me through the water, water up to the ankles.
verses.47:4: Again he measured a thousand and led me through the water, water up to the knees. Again he measured a thousand and led me through, water up to the waist.
verses.47:5: Again he measured a thousand, and it was a river that I could not cross, for the water had risen, water deep enough to swim in, a river that could not be crossed.
verses.47:6: And he said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man?" Then he led me and brought me back to the bank of the river.
verses.47:7: When I returned, look, along the bank of the river were very many trees on this side and on that side.
verses.47:8: And he said to me, "These waters flow out toward the eastern region and go down into the Arabah; then they enter the sea, being led out into the sea, and the waters will be healed.
verses.47:9: And every living creature that swarms, wherever the double river goes, will live; and there will be very many fish, because these waters go there so that the waters are healed, and everything will live wherever the river goes.
verses.47:10: Fishermen will stand beside it from En-gedi to En-eglaim; these will be places for spreading nets. Their fish will be according to their kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many.
verses.47:11: But its swamps and its marshes will not be healed; they will be given over to salt.
verses.47:12: Along the river, on its bank on this side and on that side, every kind of tree for food will grow. Its leaf will not wither and its fruit will not fail; month by month it will bear fresh fruit, because its waters flow out from the sanctuary. Its fruit will be for food, and its leaf for healing."
verses.47:13: This is what the Lord GOD says: "This is the boundary by which you shall divide the land as an inheritance for the twelve tribes of Israel: Joseph shall have two portions.
verses.47:14: You shall inherit it, each man like his brother, for I lifted My hand to give it to your fathers; and this land shall fall to you as an inheritance.
verses.47:15: This shall be the boundary of the land: on the north side, from the Great Sea by the way of Hethlon to the entrance of Zedad,
verses.47:16: Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which lies between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath, and Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
verses.47:17: Thus the boundary shall run from the sea to Hazar-enon, at the border of Damascus, and on the north, northward, is the border of Hamath. This is the north side.
verses.47:18: On the east side, between Hauran and Damascus, and between Gilead and the land of Israel along the Jordan, you shall measure from the boundary to the eastern sea. This is the east side.
verses.47:19: On the south side, southward, the boundary shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meriboth-kadesh, then along the brook to the Great Sea. This is the south side, southward.
verses.47:20: On the west side, the Great Sea shall be the boundary from the boundary up to a point opposite Lebo-hamath. This is the west side.
verses.47:21: So you shall divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.
verses.47:22: You shall divide it by lot as an inheritance for yourselves and for the sojourners who sojourn in your midst, who have fathered children in your midst. They shall be to you like the native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they shall receive an allotment by lot as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
verses.47:23: In whatever tribe the sojourner sojourns, there you shall assign his inheritance," declares the Lord GOD.
verses.48:1: Now these are the names of the tribes: From the northern end, alongside the road of Hethlon to Lebo-hamath, Hazar-enan, the boundary of Damascus northward alongside Hamath, the eastern side and the west shall belong to him: Dan, one share.
verses.48:2: And along the boundary of Dan, from the eastern side to the western side: Asher, one share.
verses.48:3: And along the boundary of Asher, from the eastern side to the western side: Naphtali, one share.
verses.48:4: And along the boundary of Naphtali, from the eastern side to the western side: Manasseh, one share.
verses.48:5: And along the boundary of Manasseh, from the eastern side to the western side: Ephraim, one share.
verses.48:6: And along the boundary of Ephraim, from the eastern side to the western side: Reuben, one share.
verses.48:7: And along the boundary of Reuben, from the eastern side to the western side: Judah, one share.
verses.48:8: And along the boundary of Judah, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be the contribution that you are to set apart: twenty-five thousand in width, and in length like one of the shares, from the eastern side to the western side; and the sanctuary shall be in the middle of it.
verses.48:9: The contribution that you are to set apart to the LORD shall be twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width.
verses.48:10: And to these shall belong the holy contribution, to the priests: on the north twenty-five thousand, and on the west ten thousand in width, and on the east ten thousand in width, and on the south twenty-five thousand in length; and the sanctuary of the LORD shall be in the middle of it.
verses.48:11: This shall belong to the consecrated priests from the sons of Zadok, who kept My charge, who did not stray when the sons of Israel strayed, just as the Levites strayed.
verses.48:12: And it shall belong to them as a dedicated contribution from the contribution of the land, most holy, next to the boundary of the Levites.
verses.48:13: And parallel to the boundary of the priests, the Levites shall have twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width; the entire length shall be twenty-five thousand, and the width ten thousand.
verses.48:14: And they shall not sell any of it, nor shall anyone exchange it, nor shall anyone transfer the best of the land, for it is holy to the LORD.
verses.48:15: And the five thousand remaining in width, fronting the twenty-five thousand, shall be unconsecrated, for the city, for dwellings and for open land; and the city shall be in the middle of it.
verses.48:16: And these are its measurements: the northern side, four thousand five hundred; and the southern side, four thousand five hundred; and on the eastern side, four thousand five hundred; and the western side, four thousand five hundred.
verses.48:17: And the city shall have open land: on the north, two hundred fifty; on the south, two hundred fifty; on the east, two hundred fifty; and on the west, two hundred fifty.
verses.48:18: And what remains in length, parallel to the holy contribution, shall be ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west, and it shall be parallel to the holy contribution; and its produce shall be for food for those who serve the city.
verses.48:19: And those from all the tribes of Israel who serve the city shall work it.
verses.48:20: The entire contribution shall be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand; as a square you shall set apart the holy contribution along with the possession of the city.
verses.48:21: And what remains shall belong to the prince, on both sides of the holy contribution and of the possession of the city, fronting the twenty-five thousand of the contribution as far as the eastern boundary, and on the west fronting the twenty-five thousand to the western boundary, parallel to the shares; it shall belong to the prince. And the holy contribution and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the middle of it.
verses.48:22: And apart from the possession of the Levites and the possession of the city, which shall be in the middle of what belongs to the prince, what lies between the boundary of Judah and the boundary of Benjamin shall belong to the prince.
verses.48:23: And the remaining tribes: from the eastern side to the western side, Benjamin, one share.
verses.48:24: And along the boundary of Benjamin, from the eastern side to the western side: Simeon, one share.
verses.48:25: And along the boundary of Simeon, from the eastern side to the western side: Issachar, one share.
verses.48:26: And along the boundary of Issachar, from the eastern side to the western side: Zebulun, one share.
verses.48:27: And along the boundary of Zebulun, from the eastern side to the western side: Gad, one share.
verses.48:28: And along the boundary of Gad, on the southern side southward, the boundary shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, to the brook, to the Great Sea.
verses.48:29: This is the land that you shall assign by lot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these are their divisions, declares the Lord GOD.
verses.48:30: And these are the exits of the city: on the northern side, four thousand five hundred in measurement.
verses.48:31: And the gates of the city shall bear the names of the tribes of Israel, three gates on the north: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
verses.48:32: And on the eastern side, four thousand five hundred, and three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
verses.48:33: And on the southern side, four thousand five hundred in measurement, and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.
verses.48:34: On the western side, four thousand five hundred; their gates are three: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
verses.48:35: All around, it shall be eighteen thousand; and from that day onward the name of the city shall be "The LORD Is There."

notes.1:4: The rare noun chashmal (occurring only in Ezek 1:4, 27; 8:2) likely denotes a luminous metal alloy such as electrum (cf. Akkadian elmeshu). The construct noun 'en (lit. 'eye') is used throughout chapter 1 for 'gleam' or 'luster,' and the Hithpael participle mithlaqqachat conveys fire continuously flaring back and forth.
notes.1:5: Throughout Ezekiel 1, masculine and feminine plural pronouns and suffixes alternate freely when referring to the four living creatures (chayyoth, grammatically feminine) and their parts.
notes.1:8: Ketiv/Qere: the Qere (read form) is widey ('and hands of'), whereas the Ketiv (written form) is wydw ('and his hand').
notes.1:15: Literally 'for its four faces'; the masculine singular suffix on panaw apparently refers distributively to each four-faced creature (or to the four fronts of the group).
notes.1:23: The Hebrew text repeats the clause 'each had two covering them,' likely emphasizing the paired wings covering each creature's body on both sides.
notes.2:2: The noun ruach ("spirit") lacks the definite article here (as also in 3:12, 14, 24; 8:3; 11:1, 24; 43:5) and can denote "a spirit," "the Spirit," or "wind." The participle middabber ("the One speaking") is a rare Hithpael form of dabar with assimilated taw.
notes.2:6: Sarabim ('briers') is a hapax legomenon, traditionally understood alongside sallonim ('thorns') as thorny briers or stubborn resisters.
notes.2:10: Hi ('woe') occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible, likely a shortened form of nehi ('wailing') or an exclamation of grief.
notes.3:5: Literally 'deep of lip and heavy of tongue,' a Hebrew idiom for people who speak an obscure, foreign language (cf. Isa 33:19).
notes.3:6: The particle 'im-lo' ('surely') introduces an emphatic statement with implied conditional force: if Ezekiel were sent to foreign nations, they would listen.
notes.3:12: Hebrew ruach lacks the definite article here and may be read as "a spirit," "the Spirit," or "wind" (cf. 2:2). The Masoretic Text reads barukh ('blessed be'), preserved here without textual emendation.
notes.3:14: Hebrew ruach ("a spirit") lacks the definite article here and may be read as "a spirit," "the Spirit," or "wind" (cf. 2:2).
notes.3:15: Ketiv/Qere: the Qere (read form) is wa'eshev ('and I dwelt/sat'), translated here as 'and I dwelt where they were dwelling,' whereas the Ketiv (written form) is wa'asher ('and where').
notes.3:24: Hebrew ruach lacks the definite article here and may be read as "a spirit," "the Spirit," or "wind" (cf. 2:2).
notes.4:6: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv reads הימיני (hayyemini), while Qere reads הַיְמָנִי (hayyemani); both are spelling variants of the adjective meaning "right."
notes.4:10: The Hebrew idiom מֵעֵת עַד־עֵת literally means "from time to time," denoting fixed daily intervals (repeated in 4:11).
notes.4:12: The verb תְּעֻגֶנָה (Qal imperfect 2ms of the rare denominative root עוג with a 3fs suffix) forms a wordplay with עֻגַת ("cake"), meaning "you shall bake it as a cake."
notes.4:15: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv reads צפועי, while Qere reads צְפִיעֵי, both spelling variants of a rare noun denoting cattle dung.
notes.5:7: Hebrew הֲמָנְכֶם (from הָמוֹן/המה, "tumult, commotion, turbulence") refers to unruly commotion; also, the Masoretic Text includes לֹא ("not") in the final clause, implying Israel failed to live up even to the surrounding nations' standards (contrast Ezek 11:12).
notes.5:11: Hebrew אֶגְרַע (Qal imperfect of גרע, "diminish, withdraw," or "shear/clip off" as in Isa 15:2) appears here without an explicit object, hence rendered "withdraw."
notes.5:13: Hebrew וְהִנֶּחָמְתִּי is a Hithpael weqatal of נחם with assimilated taw, conveying the sense of relieving oneself of anger or finding satisfaction.
notes.5:15: The Masoretic Text uses the 3rd-person feminine singular verb וְהָיְתָה ("and she will become," referring to Jerusalem) before resuming 2nd-person feminine singular address (סְבִיבוֹתָיִךְ, "around you"); similarly, 5:16 shifts from 3rd-person plural בָּהֶם ("against them") to 2nd-person plural לְשַׁחֶתְכֶם ("to destroy you").
notes.6:3: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv reads ולגיאות, while Qere reads וְלַגֵּיאָיוֹת ("and to the valleys"), a variant plural spelling of גַּיְא ("valley").
notes.6:6: Hebrew וְיֶאְשְׁמוּ (Qal imperfect of אשׁם, "bear guilt" or "suffer the penalty of guilt") forms a soundplay with תִּישָׁמְנָה (Qal imperfect of ישׁם, "become desolate") earlier in the verse.
notes.6:9: Hebrew נִשְׁבַּרְתִּי (Niphal perfect 1cs of שׁבר, "I have been broken") is unusually followed by the marker אֶת before "their heart" and "their eyes," expressing the cause or respect in which the LORD was broken.
notes.6:14: Hebrew מִמִּדְבַּר דִּבְלָתָה combines the construct noun מִדְבַּר with directional דִּבְלָתָה ("from the wilderness to Diblah," or "more than the wilderness toward Diblah"). Diblah is otherwise unknown and is often compared to Riblah in northern Syria due to the graphic similarity of ד and ר.
notes.7:2: Ketiv ארבעת (feminine construct) vs. Qere אַרְבַּע (masculine construct, standard before feminine כַּנְפוֹת, literally 'wings' or 'edges').
notes.7:4: הַצְּפִירָה ('the doom', also in 7:10) is a rare noun meaning 'cycle/turn of fate' or 'doom' (compare 'crown/wreath' in Isa 28:5); הֵד is a hapax legomenon related to הֵידָד ('joyful shouting').
notes.7:7: Native Masoretic order places 7:3–5 before 7:6–9. In the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 7:6–9 map to slots 7:3–6, MT 7:3–4 map to slots 7:7–8, and MT 7:5 is combined with 7:10 at slot 7:10 (leaving slot 7:9 unmapped).
notes.7:10: Native Masoretic order preserves MT 7:3–5 before 7:6–9 and 7:10 as a standalone verse. In the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 7:6–9 appear at slots 7:3–6, MT 7:3–4 at slots 7:7–8, there is no separate slot 7:9, and MT 7:5 ('This is what the Lord GOD says: Disaster, a singular disaster! Look, it is coming!') is combined with MT 7:10 at slot 7:10.
notes.7:11: Contains two hapax legomena of uncertain sense in elliptical verbless clauses: מֶהֱמֵהֶם ('of their abundance/wealth', or 'tumult') and נֹהַּ ('eminence/preeminence', or possibly 'wailing' from נהה).
notes.7:21: Ketiv וחללוה (third-person feminine singular suffix) vs. Qere וְחִלְּלוּהוּ (third-person masculine singular suffix, referring back to the masculine 'beauty of its ornament' in 7:20).
notes.8:2: The Masoretic Hebrew reads אֵשׁ ('fire', compare 1:27), whereas the Septuagint reflects אִישׁ ('a man'); הַחַשְׁמַלָה ('glowing metal', with paragogic -ah) is a rare term confined to Ezekiel (1:4, 27; 8:2) denoting glowing metal, electrum, or amber.
notes.8:3: Hebrew ruach lacks the definite article here and may be read as "a spirit," "the Spirit," or "wind" (cf. 2:2).
notes.8:6: Ketiv מהם (written as one word) vs. Qere מָה הֵם ('what they'); the Qal infinitive construct לְרׇחֳקָה ('to go far away') implies causing God to depart far from His sanctuary.
notes.8:11: עֲתַר is a hapax legomenon, understood either as 'aroma/fragrance' or as a 'thick, billowing mass' of incense smoke.
notes.8:16: מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶם is an anomalous conflate Masoretic form combining the Hishtaphel participle מִשְׁתַּחֲוִים ('bowing down') with a second-person plural ending -tem.
notes.8:17: 'Extending the branch to their nose' describes an obscure gesture of cultic provocation; Jewish scribal tradition lists אַפָּם ('their nose') among the tiqqunei soferim ('emendations of the scribes') for an original 'My nose'.
notes.9:1: קָרְבוּ is vocalized as a Qal perfect ('have drawn near'), though with different vocalization (קִרְבוּ or קַרְּבוּ) it is often read as an imperative ('Draw near' or 'Bring near'); פְּקֻדּוֹת ('visitations/punishments') is used concretely for the appointed executioners.
notes.9:5: Two Ketiv/Qere variants: Ketiv על ('upon' or orthographic variant) vs. Qere אַל ('do not'), and Ketiv עיניכם (plural 'your eyes') vs. Qere עֵינְכֶם (singular 'your eye', matching the feminine singular verb תָּחֹס).
notes.9:8: וְנֵאשְׁאַר is an anomalous conflate Masoretic form blending the first-person singular imperfect אֶשָּׁאֵר and the Niphal participle נִשְׁאָר ('I was left').
notes.9:9: מֻטֶּה is a hapax legomenon from the root נטה ('bend, turn aside'), denoting 'perverted justice' or 'injustice'.
notes.9:11: Ketiv כאשר ('just as') vs. Qere כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר ('according to all that').
notes.10:2: Heb. haggalgal ("the wheelwork") is a singular collective noun for the rolling wheel assembly, distinguished from the plural ʾopannim ("wheels") in vv. 9-13. Heb. chofnekha is dual, denoting both cupped hands.
notes.10:9: Heb. ʾeven tarshish is literally "stone of Tarshish," a precious stone commonly identified as beryl or chrysolite.
notes.10:12: Heb. gabbehem denotes "their backs" here alongside body, hands, and wings (the same noun denotes wheel "rims" in 1:18). The final appositional phrase leʾarbaʿtam ʾopannehem literally reads "for the four of them, their wheels."
notes.10:19: MT reads the singular verb wayyaʿamod ("and it stood"), treating the cherubim and wheels together as a single unit or resuming "the glory of the LORD" from v. 18.
notes.11:1: Hebrew ruach lacks the definite article here and may be read as "a spirit," "the Spirit," or "wind" (cf. 2:2).
notes.11:7: MT reads the Hiphil third-person masculine singular hotsiʾ (used impersonally, "one will bring out," hence "you will be brought out"), contrasting with the first-person "I will bring you out" in v. 9.
notes.11:15: Heb. ʾanshe geʾullatekha is literally "the men of your redemption," referring to relatives bound by the obligation of kinsman-redemption (compare Lev 25:25).
notes.11:16: Heb. miqdash meʿat can mean either "a sanctuary in small measure" or temporally "a sanctuary for a little while" during the exile.
notes.11:19: MT abruptly shifts to a second-person plural suffix in beqirbekhem ("within you") amid the surrounding third-person plural pronouns ("them," "their"), continuing the alternation of address from vv. 16-18.
notes.11:21: MT reads weʾel-lev shiqqutsehem ("toward the heart of their detestable things"), an unusual expression pairing the people's "heart" with the "heart" (core or desire) of their detestable practices.
notes.11:24: The first occurrence of ruach lacks the definite article ("a spirit," though "the Spirit" or "wind" is also plausible; cf. 2:2), whereas the second stands in construct with God (beruach elohim, "by the Spirit of God").
notes.12:10: The Hebrew verbless clause fronts "the prince" (הַנָּשִׂיא) without a preposition before "this burden" (הַמַּשָּׂא הַזֶּה), creating a wordplay between prophetic "burden/oracle" (מַשָּׂא) and "carry" (נָשָׂא, vv. 6-7, 12). The final suffix in בְתוֹכָם is literally 3rd-person masculine plural ("in their midst").
notes.12:12: The conjunction יַעַן אֲשֶׁר (normally causal, "because") functions here with purpose or result force ("so that"), accompanied by the emphatic pronoun הוּא ("he himself") and לַעַיִן (lit. "to/with the eye").
notes.12:19: Verses 19-20 weave a threefold wordplay on the root שׁמם: drinking "with horror" (בְּשִׁמָּמוֹן), "her land" (Jerusalem's) "will be desolated" (תֵּשַׁם), and the land becoming "a desolation" (שְׁמָמָה, v. 20).
notes.12:25: The Niphal imperfect תִמָּשֵׁךְ ("be drawn out / postponed") is 3rd-person feminine singular, used impersonally here and again in v. 28 with the masculine plural subject כׇּל־דְּבָרָי ("all My words").
notes.13:3: The negative particle לְבִלְתִּי, ordinarily used with an infinitive construct, governs the finite Qal perfect verb רָאוּ ("and have seen nothing"), a rare biblical construction.
notes.13:11: The Masoretic Text reads the 2nd-person feminine plural pronoun וְאַתֵּנָה ("and you, hailstones, will fall"), addressing the hailstones (אַבְנֵי אֶלְגָּבִישׁ) directly in apostrophe rather than reading a 1st-person verb ("I will send") as in some ancient versions.
notes.13:14: After masculine singular suffixes referring to the wall (וְהִגַּעְתִּיהוּ, יְסֹדוֹ), the Hebrew shifts abruptly to feminine singular in וְנָפְלָה ("she/it will fall") and בְּתוֹכָהּ ("in her/its midst"), pointing through the metaphor to the city of Jerusalem (cf. v. 16).
notes.13:18: The rare nouns כְּסָתוֹת ("bands," also v. 20) and מִסְפָּחוֹת ("veils," also v. 21) refer to arm bindings and head coverings used in divinatory rituals. MT's אַצִּילֵי יָדַי literally reads "joints of my hands," generally understood as a shortened dual for "joints of hands" (wrists) parallel to "the head of every stature."
notes.13:20: The Qal feminine plural participle לְפֹרְחוֹת ("like birds") reflects the late Hebrew and Aramaic sense of פרח ("fly"). The resumptive object אֶת־נְפָשִׁים preserves an unusual masculine-ending plural of נֶפֶשׁ (elsewhere נְפָשׁוֹת).
notes.14:3: The phrase "brought up their idols upon their heart" reflects the Hiphil of alah (lit. "cause to ascend"), portraying deliberate devotion to idolatry. The verb form ha-iddarosh iddaresh pairs a rare Niphal infinitive absolute (with prosthetic aleph assimilated from the following verb) with a tolerative Niphal imperfect of darash, emphasizing "Should I truly allow Myself to be inquired of?"
notes.14:4: Ketiv reads bh ("by it" or "in the matter"), whereas Qere reads ba ("coming," Qal participle of bo), translated here as "who comes." Both v. 4 and v. 7 use the Niphal of anah ("answer, respond") to stress that the LORD Himself will respond directly.
notes.14:8: The unusual verb form vahashimotihu combines the sin consonant of sim ("make, set") with the geminate Hiphil vocalization of shamem ("appall, devastate"), followed by the idiom "into a sign and bywords" (plural meshalim).
notes.14:14: Ketiv writes the name defectively as dn'l ("Danel") here and in v. 20, while Qere reads Daniyyel ("Daniel"). The verb yenatselu ("would rescue") is a rare Piel of natsal, contrasting with the standard Hiphil yatsilu in vv. 16, 18, and 20.
notes.14:17: Because cherev ("sword") is feminine singular, the 3fs verb taavor is translated as a jussive statement, "Let a sword pass through the land," rather than a second-person direct address.
notes.15:2: The comparative idiom mah-yihyeh ... mikkol-ets literally asks "what is [the wood of the vine] more than any wood?" The feminine noun hazzemorah ("the vine branch") stands in apposition to masculine ets-haggefen ("the wood of the vine"), which accounts for the masculine verb hayah ("is") that follows.
notes.15:3: In vv. 3 and 5, the verb asah ("make, work") combined with limlakhah ("for work") denotes working or employing a material for a useful craft or object.
notes.15:4: The Hebrew repeats the root akhal ("eat, consume") across vv. 4-7, pairing the noun leokhlah ("to be consumed," lit. "for food/consumption," vv. 4, 6) with the fire consuming the wood and the inhabitants of Jerusalem (vv. 4, 5, 7). Both nachar (v. 4) and vayyechar (v. 5) are Niphal forms of charar ("be charred, scorched").
notes.16:4: The noun translated "for cleansing" is a Hebrew hapax legomenon whose exact etymology is uncertain, generally understood from cognate roots as cleansing or rubbing smooth. The final two clauses pair a Hophal infinitive absolute with a passive verb (Hophal of malach, Pual of chatal) for emphatic negation.
notes.16:13: Following the qere ("fine linen" and "you ate"); the ketiv writes "my fine linen" (or a variant spelling) and an archaic second-person feminine singular ending (-ti) on the verb, a ketiv/qere pattern that recurs on the verbs in vv. 18, 22, and 31.
notes.16:16: The closing Hebrew clause is notably terse, literally "not coming things and it will not be," expressing unprecedented outrage.
notes.16:20: Following the qere plural ("your acts of prostitution"); the ketiv is singular ("your prostitution"), a variant that recurs in v. 25. In v. 21, the Hiphil of avar ("causing them to pass over") is the technical Hebrew idiom for child sacrifice by fire, though "fire" is unstated here.
notes.16:29: Hebrew eretz kenaan literally means "land of Canaan," playing on v. 3 while using kenaan in its secondary sense of "commerce" or "merchants" for Chaldea (compare 17:4).
notes.16:36: The noun translated "lust" (nechoshet) is uncertain in meaning, elsewhere denoting "bronze," and is commonly understood here from Akkadian cognates as sexual passion or lavishly spent wealth.
notes.16:43: Following the qere on both verbs (standard 2fs forms where the ketiv writes the archaic -ti ending, as also in vv. 47 and 51). The final negative clause (velo asit) is rendered as an unmarked rhetorical question matching the Qal perfect verb.
notes.16:51: Following the qere plural ("your sisters") where the ketiv consonantal spelling could be read singular; the verse also has the archaic -ti ketiv ending on the final verb.
notes.16:53: The idiom "restore the fortunes" pairs the verb shuv with shevit/shevut, where the qere reads shevut three times against the ketiv shevit. The closing phrase combines both nouns (shevut shevitayikh) emphatically.
notes.16:59: Following the qere 1cs verb ("I will deal"); the ketiv omits the final yod. In v. 57, the Hebrew text reads "Aram" (Syria), translated literally rather than emended to "Edom."
notes.17:4: Hebrew אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן ("land of Canaan") functions here as a wordplay on the sense of כְּנַעַן as "merchant" or "trade," parallel to עִיר רֹכְלִים ("city of merchants"), referring to Babylon.
notes.17:5: קָח is a rare form of לקח ("took") lacking the initial lamed; צַפְצָפָה ("willow") is a hapax legomenon, identified via Semitic cognates (cf. Arabic safsaf) as a water-loving willow.
notes.17:9: יְקוֹסֵס ("strip off") is a hapax Poel imperfect of the geminate root קסס, and לְמַשְׂאוֹת ("to pull it up") is a rare Aramaizing Qal infinitive construct of נשׂא with a mem prefix.
notes.17:21: MT מִבְרָחָו ("his fugitives," from ברח, "flee") shows a defective spelling of the plural suffix -āw and is preceded by the marker אֵת before the grammatical subject.
notes.18:10: MT וְעָשָׂה אָח מֵאַחַד מֵאֵלֶּה is syntactically compressed, literally "and does [to] a brother from one of these" (compare אָח in v. 18); some interpreters alternatively take אָח as meaning "the like of" any one of these offenses.
notes.18:14: וַיִּרְאֶה is an unapocopated Qal wayyiqtol of ראה ("see, consider"), appearing again in v. 28; some ancient versions instead read a form of ירא ("fear").
notes.18:17: MT reads מֵעָנִי ("from the poor," i.e., refraining from harming the poor), in contrast to מֵעָוֶל ("from injustice") in v. 8.
notes.18:20: Qere reads definite הָרָשָׁע ("the wicked one," matching definite הַצַּדִּיק, "the righteous one"), whereas ketiv writes anarthrous רשע.
notes.18:28: Qere reads the standard apocopated Qal wayyiqtol וַיָּשָׁב ("and turns back"), whereas ketiv writes the long form וישוב.
notes.19:5: נוֹחֲלָה is a Niphal perfect 3fs of יחל ("wait, hope"), denoting prolonged waiting in vain, parallel to אָבְדָה תִּקְוָתָהּ ("her hope had perished").
notes.19:7: MT וַיֵּדַע אַלְמְנוֹתָיו literally reads "he knew [i.e., violated] his/their widows" (with 3ms collective suffix referring to אָדָם in v. 6); many compare אַלְמְנוֹתָיו to the l/r by-form of אַרְמְנוֹתָיו ("citadels, fortresses") in Isa 13:22, parallel to "their cities."
notes.19:9: סוּגַר ("cage") is a hapax legomenon, cognate with Akkadian shigaru, denoting a wooden neck-stock, collar, or cage used to confine wild beasts or royal captives.
notes.19:10: MT reads בְּדָמְךָ ("in your blood," possibly meaning "in your bloodline" or "in your vigor"); a conjectural emendation reads בְּכַרְמְךָ ("in your vineyard").
notes.20:5: Hebrew "lifted My hand" (nasa yad) is a gesture and idiom for swearing a solemn oath, recurring throughout the chapter (20:6, 15, 23, 28, 42).
notes.20:26: The Hebrew phrase "cause everything that opens the womb to pass over" uses the Hiphil of abar (echoing Exod 13:12) and implicitly refers to child sacrifice by fire (explicit in 20:31). The Hiphil verb ashimmem (from shamem) can mean either "appall" or "devastate."
notes.20:29: The Hebrew contains a wordplay linking bamah ("high place," transliterated Bamah) with mah ("what") and baim ("going"), mocking the illegitimate cultic shrines.
notes.20:37: The noun masoret ("bond") occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and is generally derived from asar ("to bind"), denoting the binding obligation of the covenant.
notes.20:39: The Hebrew syntax of the middle clause is terse and elliptical: literally "and afterward, if you are not listening to Me," which can also be read as an oath-like assertion meaning "and afterward you will surely listen to Me."
notes.21:2: The verse uses three Hebrew terms for south (Teman, Darom, and Negev); "drop words" translates the Hiphil imperative of nataph ("drip"), an idiom for prophetic utterance.
notes.21:15: The Hebrew of the second half ("Or shall we rejoice? The scepter of My son despises every tree") is famously cryptic, with the feminine participle mo'eset ("despising") linking either to "scepter" or to the feminine "sword"; the same phrase recurs in verse 18.
notes.21:20: Hebrew ibchat ("threat" or "slaughter") is a hapax legomenon of uncertain meaning, and me'uttah is the Pual participle of 'atah ("wrapped"), sometimes understood as a variant for "polished."
notes.21:28: Ketiv reads kqswm (plene spelling) while Qere reads kiqsam ("like divining" in construct with shav', "falsehood"), which is translated here. The phrase "bound as they are by solemn oaths" translates the rare Qal passive participle construct shevu'ei followed by shevu'ot ("oaths").
notes.21:33: Hebrew lehakhil is the Hiphil infinitive construct of kul (literally "to contain" or "to hold"), used idiomatically for "to the utmost" and often understood by ancient versions as "to consume."
