notes.22:16: Hebrew wenichalt is vocalized as the Niphal of chalal ("you will be profaned"), meaning Jerusalem will suffer desecration in herself before the nations, rather than the Qal of nachal ("inherit").
notes.22:18: Ketiv reads lesug while Qere reads lesig ("for dross"), matching the plural sigim ("dross") later in this verse and in verse 19; the Qere is translated here.
notes.22:24: Hebrew gushmah is an unusual Masoretic form combining a passive verbal vocalization of gasham ("rained upon") with a final mappiq-he (as if a suffixed noun, "her rain"); the sense in context is that the land receives no rain in the day of indignation.
notes.22:25: The Masoretic Text reads qesher nevi'eha ("a conspiracy of her prophets"), which is followed here rather than the Septuagint's "her princes."
notes.23:5: MT qerovim (also v. 12) is the plural of qarov ("near, nearby"), referring to Assyrian officials stationed in neighboring territories; some scholars instead link it to Aramaic or Akkadian roots meaning "warriors." Hebrew tachtai literally means "under Me," an idiom for being under a husband's authority.
notes.23:21: Follows the Masoretic text directly: ba'asot (Qal infinitive construct of 'asah II, "handle, fondle," cf. Piel in vv. 3, 8) with partitive mi-Mitsrayim ("those from Egypt") and lema'an ("on account of").
notes.23:24: Hebrew hotsen occurs only here in the Bible and is traditionally understood as "weapons" or "armaments."
notes.23:42: Follows the Qere ("Sabeans"); the Ketiv reads sove'im (Qal participle of sava', "drunkards").
notes.23:43: Follows the Qere 'attah yiznu ("now they will practice prostitution," Qal imperfect 3mp of zanah); the Ketiv reads 'et ("time") and yizneh (3ms). The terse final word vehi literally reads "and she."
notes.24:2: Ketiv/Qere orthographic variant: the ketiv is spelled plene (ktwb) and the qere defectively (ktb) before the maqqef; both represent the Qal masculine singular imperative of katav ("write").
notes.24:5: MT reads "the bones" (ha-atsamim), not "the wood" (ha-etsim), maintaining the stark imagery of the pot; the preceding laqoach ("take") is a Qal infinitive absolute used imperatively.
notes.24:12: The opening clause te'unim hel'at ("she has exhausted efforts") is notably terse and preserves the archaic third-person feminine singular Hiphil ending -at on la'ah ("weary, exhaust"). The closing verbless clause be'esh chel'atah ("into the fire with her corrosion!") may alternatively indicate that her corrosion will not come out even by fire.
notes.24:14: MT reads the third-person plural Qal perfect shefatukh ("they will judge you," an indefinite plural or reference to the Babylonian invaders), rather than first-person singular "I will judge you."
notes.24:22: Within Ezekiel's recounting of the LORD's message, the voice briefly shifts in verses 22-23 into Ezekiel's own first-person perspective ("as I have done") before returning to third-person reference to Ezekiel in verse 24. "The bread of men" (also in v. 17) refers to consolation food customarily brought to mourners.
notes.25:7: Ketiv/Qere variant: the qere reads levaz ("as plunder," matching 26:5), whereas the ketiv reads levag (either a rare loanword for "food/portion" or a scribal confusion of gimel and zayin).
notes.25:9: Ketiv/Qere variant: the qere reads the dual place-name ve-Qiryataymah ("and Kiriathaim," with final -ah), whereas the ketiv wqrytmh omits the yod.
notes.25:16: The Hebrew employs a wordplay between the Hiphil verb vehikhratti ("and I will cut off," root krt) and the gentilic name Keretim ("Cherethites").
notes.26:7: The Hebrew spells the Babylonian king's name Nevukhadretstsar (closer to Akkadian Nabu-kudurri-usur), rendered here with the standard English spelling Nebuchadnezzar.
notes.26:9: The phrase mechi qavollo ("the blow of his battering ram") consists of two hapax legomena from roots meaning "strike" and "be opposite/in front." "His axes" renders charvotav, literally "his swords" or "iron blades," here iron demolition tools (cf. Exod 20:25).
notes.26:17: MT reads the Niphal participle noshevet miyyammim ("inhabited from the seas," i.e., populated by seafaring peoples) and repeats yosheveha ("her inhabitants") at the close of the verse, referring to the inhabitants of the surrounding maritime region or Tyre's dependencies.
notes.26:20: MT reads venatatti tsevi be'erets chayyim ("and I will set glory in the land of the living"), contrasting Tyre's descent to the pit with God's establishment of splendor among the living.
notes.27:3: Ketiv hyšbty preserves an archaic feminine participle ending (-i), while Qere hayyōšebet is the standard Qal active participle feminine singular ("who sits"); the translation follows the Qere.
notes.27:6: MT bat-ʾăšurîm (literally "daughter of boxwoods") is widely understood as a word-division variant for bĕtaʾăšurîm ("in boxwood," cf. Isa 41:19; 60:13).
notes.27:15: Ketiv whwbnm and Qere wĕhobnîm ("and ebony") are orthographic variants of the same plural noun; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.27:17: Hebrew pannag is a hapax legomenon of uncertain meaning, likely referring to a type of fine meal or baked confection (cf. Akkadian pannigu).
notes.27:19: MT wĕdān may be read either as the Arabian place name "Vedan" or as "and Dan," and mĕʾuzzāl either as "from Uzal" (cf. Gen 10:27) or as a Pual participle meaning "spun yarn."
notes.28:3: Ketiv mdnʾl spells the name defectively ("Danel"), while Qere middānîyyēʾl reads the standard form "Daniel"; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.28:12: MT ḥōtēm tāknît uses the Qal active participle of ḥātam ("sealing up") with tāknît ("proportion, measurement," cf. 43:10), conveying "one who sets the seal on perfection"; many also take ḥōtēm as a construct form of ḥōtām ("seal/signet of perfection").
notes.28:13: The phrase tuppêkā ûnĕqābêkā literally refers to "your tambourines" (tōp) and "your pipes" or "perforations" (neqeb, a hapax common noun from nāqab, "to pierce"), though in proximity to gold and gemstones it is often interpreted as jewelry "settings and sockets."
notes.28:14: MT reads ʾatt-kĕrûb mimšaḥ hassōkēk ("You were an anointed, overshadowing cherub"), using the defective spelling ʾatt for the masculine singular pronoun "you" (cf. Num 11:15; Deut 5:27) rather than the preposition "with" (ʾēt); the hapax noun mimšaḥ is usually derived from māšaḥ ("anoint"), though some connect it to an Aramaic cognate meaning "outstretched."
notes.28:16: MT wāʾabbedkā is a Piel first-person singular wayyiqtol of ʾābad ("and I destroyed you") with contracted initial ʾālep, addressing the cherub directly.
notes.29:3: Hebrew tannim is a singular spelling variant of tannin, referring to a great aquatic monster or chaos dragon. The verb asitini, Qal perfect 1cs with a 1cs suffix, is translated here as a dative suffix meaning made it for myself, parallel to 29:9, though it can also be read reflexively as I made myself.
notes.29:4: Follows the qere hachim, hooks, rather than the ketiv spelling hachayim.
notes.29:7: Follows the qere bakkaf, with the hand, rather than the ketiv bekappekha, by your hand. The final verb wehaamadta is a Hiphil of amad, literally bring to a standstill; many scholars see metathesis for the root maad, cause to shake, as in Psalm 69:24.
notes.29:10: Migdol lay near Egypt's northeastern frontier and Syene, Hebrew Seveneh with a directional suffix meaning to Syene, lay at its southern frontier bordering Cush.
notes.29:19: Hebrew hamon carries both the sense of wealth or abundance, as here and in 30:4, and teeming multitude or horde, as in 30:10, 30:15, 31:2, and 31:18.
notes.30:13: The Masoretic Hebrew names of the Egyptian cities in 30:13-18 are retained directly: Noph is Memphis, No is Thebes, Sin is Pelusium, and Aven is On or Heliopolis, vocalized as aven, wickedness, as a deliberate wordplay.
notes.30:16: Follows the qere tachul, will writhe, Qal imperfect 3fs of chul, rather than the ketiv spelling tachil. The closing phrase tsare yomam is an elliptical construct-before-adverb construction literally meaning adversaries by day.
notes.30:17: Hebrew wehennah is a feminine plural pronoun referring back to the cities Aven and Pi-beseth, since cities are grammatically feminine in Hebrew.
notes.30:18: The Masoretic text writes chasak with sin instead of chashak with shin, grow dark, an orthographic variant supported by the following reference to a covering cloud. Hebrew motot, yoke bars, follows the Masoretic vocalization rather than the Septuagint reading scepters.
notes.31:3: Hebrew avotim in 31:3, 31:10, and 31:14 is morphologically a plural of avot, dense or intertwined boughs, as in Ezekiel 19:11, though ancient versions render it clouds by connecting it to av.
notes.31:10: The Masoretic text shifts abruptly from second-person masculine singular gavahta, you towered, directly addressing the royal figure, to third-person masculine singular forms for the rest of the verse.
notes.31:14: Hebrew elehem is pointed with an initial tsere as the plural noun el or ayil with a suffix, their mighty ones or mighty trees, rather than the preposition alehem, to them.
notes.31:15: Hebrew ulpeh is a rare Pual-patterned stative or nominal form from the root alaph, meaning grew faint or wilted.
notes.31:17: Hebrew uzeroo literally means and its arm, referring collectively to the empire's military allies or supporters, which accounts for the plural verb yashevu, dwelt.
notes.32:2: The verb nidmeta is taken as Niphal of damah II ("be ruined/undone"), with "young lion of the nations" as vocative, since damah I ("resemble") is unattested elsewhere in Niphal and normally takes a preposition; alternatively, from damah I, "You have likened yourself to a young lion of the nations."
notes.32:5: Hebrew ramuteka is a hapax legomenon from the root rum ("be high"), literally "your height," denoting the monster's towering bulk or massive carcass.
notes.32:6: Hebrew tsafateka is a hapax legomenon from tsuf ("flow/overflow"), construed here as a second object ("your outflow") clarified by "with your blood"; alternatively, a construct phrase, "the land of your swimming."
notes.32:27: Translates the Masoretic Hebrew directly: me'arelim ("from among the uncircumcised") and avonotam ("their iniquities," a plural noun with a preceding 3fs verb).
notes.32:32: Translates the Masoretic Qere chittiti ("My terror"); the written Ketiv reads chittito ("his terror").
notes.33:12: Hebrew bah ("by it") is feminine singular, referring back unambiguously to feminine tsedeqah ("righteousness") rather than the nearer masculine resha ("wickedness").
notes.33:25: Hebrew al-haddam ("with the blood") is the cultic and dietary idiom for eating meat without draining its blood, prohibited in Leviticus 19:26.
notes.33:30: Hebrew chad ("one") is an Aramaicized form of standard Hebrew echad, occurring only here in the Hebrew text of the Old Testament.
notes.33:32: Masoretic vocalization reads shir agavim ("a song of passionate love," echoing agavim in v. 31), followed by personal qualifiers describing a skilled singer and musician.
notes.34:2: The Hebrew verb ra'ah ('tend, shepherd, feed') creates wordplay with ro'im ('shepherds'): instead of tending the flock, Israel's leaders have been tending and feeding themselves (v. 3).
notes.34:12: The noun baqqarah ('looking after, inspection') occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible, and niphrashot ('scattered') is the sole Niphal occurrence of parash.
notes.34:16: The Masoretic Text reads 'I will destroy' (Hiphil imperfect of shamad), contrasting judgment on the oppressive sheep with care for the vulnerable; several ancient versions (including the Septuagint) instead reflect 'I will guard' (from shamar).
notes.34:18: The noun mishqa' ('clear water', literally 'settled water', from shaqa', 'sink/settle') and the noun mirpas in v. 19 ('what is muddied', from raphas) each appear only here in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.34:29: Literally 'a planting for a name,' meaning a renowned planting; the Masoretic Text reads leshem ('for renown'), whereas the Septuagint reflects 'of peace.'
notes.35:5: Literally 'poured out the sons of Israel onto the hands of the sword,' an idiom for delivering them over to slaughter; 'final punishment' translates 'avon qets, literally 'iniquity/punishment of the end.'
notes.35:6: The Hebrew clause 'im-lo' dam sane'ta (literally 'if you did not hate blood') is grammatically difficult and is taken causally here ('since you did not hate bloodshed'), contrasting with the affirmative oath particle 'im-lo' elsewhere.
notes.35:9: Following the Qere tashovnah ('will not be restored/return', Qal imperfect of shuv); the Ketiv teyshavnah (from yashav) reads 'will not be inhabited.'
notes.35:12: Following the Qere shamemu ('they have become desolate', 3rd-person plural Qal perfect of shamem), agreeing with 'the mountains of Israel'; the Ketiv reads the singular shamemah ('it has become desolate' or 'desolation').
notes.36:3: The forms shammot (an unusual infinitive construct of shamam used transitively, making desolate) and sha'oph (Qal infinitive absolute of sha'aph, crushing or trampling) function together with an indefinite subject; literally "upon the lip of a tongue" is a Hebrew idiom for gossip or slanderous talk.
notes.36:5: Literally "in order that its open pastureland for plunder," with an implied verb; the Masoretic vocalization migrashah points the word as the noun migrash (open or pastureland) with a feminine suffix, though some construe it as an Aramaizing infinitive of garash (to expel or empty).
notes.36:13: Here and in vv. 14-15, the Qere reads plural goyayikh ("your nations"), while the Ketiv reads singular goyekh ("your nation"); in v. 13 the Qere also reads standard feminine singular at ("you") for the archaic Ketiv spelling atti.
notes.36:14: The Qere reads teshakkeli (Piel of shakhal, "bereave"), matching vv. 12-13, whereas the Ketiv reads takhshili (from kashal, "cause to stumble"), matching the Hiphil verb takhshili in v. 15.
notes.37:9: The Hebrew noun ruach carries a deliberate triple wordplay across vv. 1-14, shifting between "Spirit" (vv. 1, 14), "breath" (vv. 5-6, 8-10), and "winds" (arba' ruchot, "four winds," v. 9).
notes.37:17: The form la'achadim is the rare plural of echad ("one"), literally "into ones," expressing complete unity; qarav is an unusual transitive imperative ("join together" or "bring near").
notes.37:22: The Qere reads plural yihyu ("they will be"), matching the plural verbs in the verse, while the Ketiv reads singular yihyeh ("it will be"), agreeing with the collective "one nation."
notes.37:23: The Masoretic text reads moshvoteihem ("their dwelling places"); the Septuagint reflects a different reading, meshuvoteihem ("their apostasies" or "backslidings").
notes.38:2: Hebrew nesi rosh (literally "prince of the head") is rendered here as "chief prince," with Meshech and Tubal paired as in 27:13 and 32:26; alternatively, taking rosh as a proper noun yields "prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal."
notes.38:12: Hebrew tabbur literally means "navel," an idiom denoting the center or highest point of the land or earth (cf. Judges 9:37). The 2nd-person masculine singular suffix on yadekha ("your hand") shows that Gog's direct speech ends at v. 11.
notes.38:13: Hebrew kefireha literally means "its young lions," a recurring metaphor in Ezekiel for proud rulers or warriors (cf. 19:3; 32:2).
notes.38:18: Hebrew be'appi literally means "in My nose" or "in My nostrils," a vivid anatomical idiom for burning anger.
notes.39:2: The Piel verb shishetikha is a hapax legomenon of uncertain meaning; in this sequence of verbs it is understood as "lead you forward" or "drive you on"; a derivation from shesh ("six"), "leave a sixth part of you," has also been proposed.
notes.39:11: Masoretic meqom-sham qever literally reads "a place there of a grave" (i.e., a burial place there). The name Hamon-gog means "Multitude of Gog," anticipating the city name Hamonah ("Multitude") in v. 16.
notes.39:14: In meqabberim et-ha'overim et-hannotarim, the first et is the preposition "with" (joining the buriers with those passing through, as described in v. 15), while the second et marks the direct object "those left."
notes.39:25: Ketiv reads shevit ("captivity"), while Qere reads shevut ("fortunes" or "restoration," in the idiom "restore the fortunes of"); the translation follows the Qere.
notes.39:26: Masoretic venasu (pointed with sin and spelled without aleph) is the Qal of nasa ("bear"), matching Ezekiel's recurring idiom "bear disgrace" (cf. 16:52, 54); some emend to shin from nashah ("forget").
notes.40:8: The Masoretic Text preserves this measurement of the vestibule toward the house (one reed) alongside the eight-cubit measurement in v. 9. The phrase mehabbayit (literally 'from the house,' vv. 7-9) indicates the inner side facing the temple house.
notes.40:14: The Hebrew syntax is compressed and difficult: wayya'as ('he made,' Qal of 'asah) appears to mean 'he reckoned' or 'measured out,' and the second clause literally reads 'and to the jamb of the court, the gate all around.'
notes.40:15: Translated from the qere ha'iton ('the entrance,' a rare noun from 'atah, 'to come'); the ketiv hy'twn is a variant consonantal spelling.
notes.40:43: The rare dual noun shefattayim is uncertain in meaning, referring either to double-pronged hooks or to ledges fastened around the inside of the slaughtering area.
notes.40:44: The Masoretic Text literally reads 'chambers for singers' (lishkot sharim) and 'the east gate' (sha'ar haqqadim), whereas the Septuagint reads 'two chambers' and 'the south gate.'
notes.41:1: The Masoretic Text literally reads "the width of the tent," an unusual phrase echoing tabernacle language; the Septuagint diverges here.
notes.41:6: Hebrew literally reads "three and thirty times"; in light of the three stories in 41:7 this is often understood as three stories of thirty side rooms each.
notes.41:8: The Qere reads "foundations" (musdot), whereas the Ketiv spells the word with yod instead of waw. The rare term atsilah literally means "to the joint," often understood as six long cubits or up to the joining point of the side rooms.
notes.41:15: The Qere reads "and its galleries" (we-attiqeha, spelled with yod to match 41:16), whereas the Ketiv spells the stem with waw.
notes.41:20: The Masoretic Text places extraordinary scribal dots (puncta extraordinaria) over the final word "the temple hall" (hahekal), marking textual uncertainty, likely because 41:21 immediately begins with the same word.
notes.42:4: The Masoretic Text reads "a passage of one cubit" (derekh ammah achat), whereas the Septuagint reflects "a length of a hundred cubits."
notes.42:9: Two Ketiv/Qere variants occur here: the Qere redivides the first phrase as "and below these chambers" and reads the Hiphil participle "the entryway" (hammevi) where the Ketiv has the noun "the entrance" (hammavo).
notes.42:10: The Masoretic Text reads "toward the east" (derekh haqqadim), whereas the Septuagint reads "toward the south," anticipating the south chambers in 42:12.
notes.42:12: The rare word haginah ("matching") occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; its exact sense is uncertain, though cognates suggest "corresponding," "suitable," or "directly opposite."
notes.42:16: The Qere reads "reeds" (qanim), aligning with 42:17-19, whereas the Ketiv reads "cubits" (ammot), which agrees with the Septuagint and the scale of chapters 40-41.
notes.43:3: MT reads first-person bebo'i ("when I came"), expressing Ezekiel's prophetic participation in the vision of Jerusalem's destruction (cf. ch. 9), whereas some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions read third-person "when He came."
notes.43:5: Hebrew ruach lacks the definite article here and may be read as "a spirit," "the Spirit," or "wind" (cf. 2:2).
notes.43:7: The direct object marker 'et precedes "the place of My throne" without a governing verb, functioning presentatively ("this is"). At the end of the verse, MT vocalizes bamotam ("their high places," used locatively or denoting royal funerary shrines), whereas repointing the consonants to bemotam yields "at their death."
notes.43:13: Hebrew cheq (lit. "bosom" or "hollow") denotes the recessed base or drainage gutter around the altar. MT gav ("back," "mound," or "pedestal") is retained here rather than emending to "height" (govah) with the Septuagint.
notes.43:15: Hebrew uses two related terms for the altar hearth: har'el and Qere 'ari'el (also in 43:16), where the Ketiv transposes the yod and 'alef ('r'yl) while the Qere reads 'ry'l.
notes.43:26: Hebrew umille'u yadav (lit. "and they shall fill its hands," with defective suffix spelling) applies the standard priestly consecration idiom ("fill the hand," cf. Exod 29:9) uniquely to the altar.
notes.44:3: The initial direct object marker 'et introduces "the prince" as a fronted topic ("As for the prince"). The Qere le'ekhol- binds "to eat" with maqqef to "bread" in defective spelling, whereas the Ketiv writes the Qal infinitive construct plene (l'kwl).
notes.44:7: MT reads third-person plural wayyaferu ("and they broke," Hiphil wayyiqtol of parar), shifting from second-person plural address; some ancient versions harmonize to second-person "you broke."
notes.44:18: Hebrew bayyaza' (lit. "in/with sweat," a hapax legomenon) refers to garments or belts that induce perspiration during priestly service.
notes.44:24: Two Ketiv/Qere variants occur here: Qere lemishpat ("for judgment") vs. Ketiv lshpt ("to judge," Qal infinitive construct), and Qere yishpetuhu ("they shall judge it," Qal imperfect) vs. Ketiv wshpthw ("and they shall judge it," Qal weqatal).
notes.44:28: The feminine singular verb wehayetah ("and it/this shall be") has no explicit subject, either functioning cataphorically to introduce "I am their inheritance" or agreeing by attraction with the feminine predicate noun nachalah ("inheritance").
notes.45:1: The unit of length is omitted in the Hebrew text here and in verses 3, 5, and 6 (likely cubits by comparison with 45:2); the noun "length" is also repeated resumptively around the numeral twenty-five thousand.
notes.45:3: The qere reads the masculine numeral "chamishah" ("five", matching the standard construction with "thousand"), whereas the ketiv writes the feminine form "chamesh".
notes.45:5: The qere reads the waw-consecutive Qal perfect "vehayah" ("shall belong"), whereas the ketiv reads the imperfect "yihyeh". The Masoretic Text explicitly reads "twenty chambers" ("esrim leshakot").
notes.45:12: The Masoretic Text lists three sub-weights totaling sixty shekels (20 + 25 + 15) for the mina, reflecting a sexagesimal weight standard.
notes.45:21: The Hebrew reads "shevu'ot yamim" (vocalized as plural of "shavua", literally "weeks of days"), functioning here in context as a seven-day period, matching "the seven days of the festival" in verse 23.
notes.46:9: The qere reads the singular Qal imperfect "yetse" ("he shall go out", agreeing with the singular subject), whereas the ketiv reads the plural "yets'u" ("they shall go out").
notes.46:15: The qere reads the Qal imperfect "ya'asu" ("they shall prepare"), whereas the ketiv reads the waw-consecutive Qal perfect "ve'asu" ("and they shall prepare").
notes.46:19: The qere reads the dual "bayyarkatayim" ("at the extreme rear"), whereas the ketiv reads "beyarkatam" (either "at their far end" or a defective dual spelling).
notes.46:22: The Qal passive participle "qeturot" is a biblical hapax legomenon, traditionally understood as "enclosed" or "unroofed" courts. The final word "mehuqtsa'ot" (Hophal participle, "set in the corners") carries Masoretic extraordinary points (puncta extraordinaria) above its letters.
notes.47:8: The Hophal participle "hammutsa'im" (from "yatsa", literally "those brought out / led forth") describes the temple waters discharging into the sea so that its waters are healed.
notes.47:9: The Hebrew uses the dual form "nachalayim" (literally "two rivers" or "double river") with a singular verb, emphasizing the great volume of the stream.
notes.47:10: The qere reads the Qal perfect "amedu" following "vehayah" ("will stand"), whereas the ketiv reads the Qal imperfect "ya'amdu".
notes.47:12: The qere reads the singular Qal perfect "vehayah" (agreeing with singular "its fruit"), whereas the ketiv reads the plural "vehayu".
notes.47:13: The demonstrative "geh" ("this") occurs only here in the Masoretic Text as a variant of "zeh" (cf. verse 15). "Two portions" renders the elliptic Hebrew "Yosef chavalim" (literally "Joseph, portions"), reflecting Ephraim and Manasseh.
notes.47:20: Literally "the entrance of Hamath," the same northern border town named "Lebo-hamath" in 48:1.
notes.48:8: The Hebrew text omits the unit of measurement throughout chapter 48; the figures are traditionally understood as cubits.
notes.48:11: Hebrew uses a collective singular Pual participle, literally 'the consecrated one,' in apposition to the plural 'priests.'
notes.48:14: Translates the qere (Hiphil imperfect, 'transfer'); the ketiv reads the Qal imperfect ('pass over'), making 'the best of the land' the grammatical subject.
notes.48:16: The Masoretic Text contains a written dittography of 'five' in the southern measurement that is marked as ketiv velo qere (written, not read) and therefore omitted in translation.
notes.48:28: The Hebrew form rendered 'to the brook' is pointed like the noun 'inheritance,' though in this southern border formula it represents 'brook/wadi' with a directional ending, referring to the Wadi of Egypt.

unplaced.text: And the living creatures were darting back and forth, like the appearance of a lightning flash.
And each one had four faces: the first face was the face of the cherub, the second face was the face of a human being, the third was the face of a lion, and the fourth was the face of an eagle.
And they will shave themselves bald for you and wrap themselves in sackcloth; they will weep over you in bitterness of soul with bitter lamentation.
Whom do you surpass in loveliness? Go down and be made to lie with the uncircumcised.
You have depended on your sword, you have committed abomination, and each one of you has defiled his neighbor's wife; should you then possess the land?
unplaced.note: Hebrew literally reads "stood upon your sword" and uses a feminine plural verb form for "you have committed."

unplaced.text: And there were vestibules all around; the length was twenty-five cubits, and the width was five cubits.

native_verses.1:1: Now it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, while I was in the midst of the exiles by the Chebar River, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
native_verses.1:2: On the fifth day of the month—it was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin—
native_verses.1:3: the word of the LORD indeed came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the Chebar River, and the hand of the LORD came upon him there.
native_verses.1:4: And I looked, and look, a tempestuous wind was coming from the north, a great cloud with fire flaring back and forth and brightness all around it; and from its midst was something like the gleam of electrum, from the midst of the fire.
native_verses.1:5: And from its midst came the likeness of four living creatures. Now this was their appearance: they had the likeness of a man.
native_verses.1:6: Each one had four faces, and each one of them had four wings.
native_verses.1:7: Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the sole of a calf's foot, and they sparkled like the gleam of burnished bronze.
native_verses.1:8: Human hands were under their wings on their four sides, and the four of them had their faces and their wings.
native_verses.1:9: Their wings were joined one to another. They did not turn as they went; each one went in the direction it faced.
native_verses.1:10: And the likeness of their faces was the face of a man; and the four of them had the face of a lion on the right side, and the four of them had the face of an ox on the left side, and the four of them had the face of an eagle.
native_verses.1:11: And their faces and their wings were spread apart above: each had two that joined another, and two that covered their bodies.
native_verses.1:12: And each one went in the direction it faced; wherever the spirit was to go, they went; they did not turn as they went.
native_verses.1:13: As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches; it was moving back and forth among the living creatures, and the fire had brightness, and lightning was coming out from the fire.
native_verses.1:14: And the living creatures were darting back and forth, like the appearance of a lightning flash.
native_verses.1:15: And I looked at the living creatures, and look, there was one wheel on the earth beside the living creatures, for its four faces.
native_verses.1:16: The appearance of the wheels and their construction was like the gleam of beryl, and the four of them had one likeness; and their appearance and their construction were as if a wheel were inside a wheel.
native_verses.1:17: Toward any of their four sides they would go as they went; they did not turn as they went.
native_verses.1:18: As for their rims, they were high and awe-inspiring, and their rims were full of eyes all around on the four of them.
native_verses.1:19: And when the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.
native_verses.1:20: Wherever the spirit was to go, they went, there where the spirit was to go; and the wheels were lifted up alongside them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
native_verses.1:21: When those went, these went; and when those stood still, these stood still; and when they were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up alongside them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
native_verses.1:22: And over the heads of the living creatures was the likeness of an expanse, like the gleam of awesome crystal, stretched out over their heads above.
native_verses.1:23: And under the expanse their wings were straight, one toward another; each had two covering them, and each had two covering their bodies.
native_verses.1:24: And I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, when they went—a sound of tumult like the sound of an army; when they stood still, they lowered their wings.
native_verses.1:25: And a voice came from above the expanse that was over their heads; when they stood still, they lowered their wings.
native_verses.1:26: And above the expanse that was over their heads was something like the appearance of a sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne; and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness with the appearance of a man, above upon it.
native_verses.1:27: And I saw something like the gleam of electrum, like the appearance of fire enclosed within it all around, from the appearance of His waist and upward; and from the appearance of His waist and downward I saw something like the appearance of fire, and there was brightness all around Him.
native_verses.1:28: Like the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud on a day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. That was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And I saw it, and I fell on my face, and I heard a voice speaking.
native_verses.2:1: Then He said to me, "Son of man, stand on your feet, so that I may speak with you."
native_verses.2:2: And a spirit came into me as He spoke to me, and stood me on my feet; and I heard the One speaking to me.
native_verses.2:3: Then He said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the sons of Israel, to rebellious nations who have rebelled against Me; they and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day.
native_verses.2:4: And the children are defiant of face and hard of heart; I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.'
native_verses.2:5: And as for them, whether they listen or refrain—for they are a house of rebellion—they will know that a prophet has been in their midst.
native_verses.2:6: And you, son of man, do not fear them, and do not fear their words, though briers and thorns are with you and you sit among scorpions. Do not fear their words and do not be dismayed at their presence, for they are a house of rebellion.
native_verses.2:7: And you shall speak My words to them, whether they listen or refrain, for they are rebellious.
native_verses.2:8: And you, son of man, listen to what I am speaking to you; do not be rebellious like the house of rebellion. Open your mouth wide and eat what I am giving you."
native_verses.2:9: Then I looked, and see, a hand was extended toward me; and look, in it was a written scroll.
native_verses.2:10: And He spread it out before me, and it was written on front and back; and written on it were laments, and groaning, and woe.
native_verses.3:1: And He said to me, "Son of man, what you find, eat—eat this scroll, and go speak to the house of Israel."
native_verses.3:2: And I opened my mouth, and He made me eat this scroll.
native_verses.3:3: And He said to me, "Son of man, feed your stomach and fill your inward parts with this scroll that I am giving you." So I ate it, and it was in my mouth like honey for sweetness.
native_verses.3:4: Then He said to me, "Son of man, go, go in to the house of Israel and speak with My words to them.
native_verses.3:5: For you are not being sent to a people deep of speech and heavy of tongue, but to the house of Israel—
native_verses.3:6: not to many peoples deep of speech and heavy of tongue, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
native_verses.3:7: Yet the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, because they are not willing to listen to Me; for all the house of Israel are hard of forehead and stubborn of heart.
native_verses.3:8: Look, I have made your face hard against their faces, and your forehead hard against their foreheads.
native_verses.3:9: Like diamond, harder than flint, I have made your forehead. Do not fear them, and do not be dismayed at their presence, for they are a house of rebellion."
native_verses.3:10: And He said to me, "Son of man, all My words that I will speak to you, take into your heart and hear with your ears.
native_verses.3:11: And go, go in to the exiles, to the sons of your people, and speak to them and say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says,' whether they listen or refrain."
native_verses.3:12: Then a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from His place!"
native_verses.3:13: And there was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing one against another, and the sound of the wheels alongside them, and the sound of a great rumbling.
native_verses.3:14: So a spirit lifted me up and took me away; and I went bitter in the fury of my spirit, while the hand of the LORD pressed hard upon me.
native_verses.3:15: Then I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who were dwelling by the Chebar River, and I dwelt where they were dwelling; and I sat there seven days, stunned, in their midst.
native_verses.3:16: And it happened at the end of seven days that the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
native_verses.3:17: "Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel; and you shall hear a word from My mouth and warn them from Me.
native_verses.3:18: When I say to the wicked man, 'You shall surely die,' and you do not warn him and do not speak to warn the wicked man from his wicked way to keep him alive, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood from your hand.
native_verses.3:19: Yet if you warn the wicked man, and he does not turn from his wickedness and from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity, but you have delivered your life.
native_verses.3:20: And when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits injustice, and I place a stumbling block before him, he shall die; because you did not warn him, he shall die in his sin, and his righteous deeds that he has done shall not be remembered, but I will require his blood from your hand.
native_verses.3:21: Yet if you warn the righteous man that the righteous man should not sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live because he took warning, and you have delivered your life."
native_verses.3:22: And the hand of the LORD came upon me there, and He said to me, "Get up, go out to the valley, and I will speak with you there."
native_verses.3:23: So I got up and went out to the valley, and look, the glory of the LORD was standing there, like the glory that I had seen by the Chebar River, and I fell on my face.
native_verses.3:24: Then a spirit came into me and stood me on my feet, and He spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself inside your house.
native_verses.3:25: And as for you, son of man, look, they will put cords on you and bind you with them, and you will not go out among them.
native_verses.3:26: And I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, and you will become mute and will not be to them a man who reproves, for they are a house of rebellion.
native_verses.3:27: Yet when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Let the one who listens listen, and let the one who refrains refrain,' for they are a house of rebellion."
native_verses.4:1: "Now you, son of man, take for yourself a brick, set it in front of you, and inscribe on it a city, Jerusalem.
native_verses.4:2: Lay siege against it, build a siege wall against it, heap up a siege ramp against it, set camps against it, and position battering rams against it all around.
native_verses.4:3: And you, take for yourself an iron griddle and set it as an iron wall between you and the city, and direct your face toward it; it shall be under siege, and you shall besiege it. It is a sign to the house of Israel.
native_verses.4:4: And you, lie down on your left side and put the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it. For the number of days that you lie on it, you shall bear their iniquity.
native_verses.4:5: And I have appointed for you the years of their iniquity as a number of days, three hundred and ninety days; so you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
native_verses.4:6: When you have finished these, you shall lie down on your right side a second time and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah for forty days; a day for each year, a day for each year I have appointed it for you.
native_verses.4:7: And toward the siege of Jerusalem you shall direct your face, with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.
native_verses.4:8: Now look, I have placed cords upon you, so that you will not turn from side to side until you have finished the days of your siege.
native_verses.4:9: And you, take for yourself wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt, and place them in one vessel and make them into bread for yourself. For the number of days that you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days, you shall eat it.
native_verses.4:10: And the food that you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; from set time to set time you shall eat it.
native_verses.4:11: And water you shall drink by measure, a sixth of a hin; from set time to set time you shall drink.
native_verses.4:12: And as a barley cake you shall eat it; you shall bake it on dung of human excrement before their eyes."
native_verses.4:13: Then the LORD said, "In this way the sons of Israel will eat their bread unclean among the nations to which I will drive them."
native_verses.4:14: Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Look, my soul has not been defiled; from my youth until now I have not eaten an animal that died naturally or was torn by beasts, nor has foul meat entered my mouth."
native_verses.4:15: Then He said to me, "See, I have given you cattle dung in place of human dung, and you shall make your bread over it."
native_verses.4:16: And He said to me, "Son of man, look, I am breaking the staff of bread in Jerusalem; they will eat bread by weight and with anxiety, and they will drink water by measure and in horror,
native_verses.4:17: so that they will lack bread and water, and be horrified, each man and his brother, and waste away in their iniquity."
native_verses.5:1: "Now you, son of man, take for yourself a sharp sword; as a barber's razor you shall take it for yourself and pass it over your head and over your beard. Then take for yourself weighing scales and divide the hair.
native_verses.5:2: A third you shall burn in the fire in the middle of the city when the days of the siege are fulfilled. And you shall take a third and strike it with the sword all around it, and a third you shall scatter to the wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.
native_verses.5:3: And you shall take from there a few in number and tie them in the corners of your garment.
native_verses.5:4: And from these you shall take some again, throw them into the middle of the fire, and burn them in the fire; from it fire will go out to the whole house of Israel."
native_verses.5:5: This is what the Lord GOD says, "This is Jerusalem; I have placed her in the midst of the nations, with lands all around her.
native_verses.5:6: Yet she has rebelled against My ordinances in wickedness beyond the nations, and against My statutes beyond the lands around her; for My ordinances they have rejected, and in My statutes they have not walked."
native_verses.5:7: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says, "Because your tumult is greater than that of the nations around you, and you have not walked in My statutes, nor carried out My ordinances, nor acted according to the ordinances of the nations around you—"
native_verses.5:8: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says, "Look, I Myself also am against you, and I will carry out judgments in your midst before the eyes of the nations.
native_verses.5:9: And I will do among you what I have not done, and anything like it I will never do again, because of all your abominations.
native_verses.5:10: Therefore fathers will eat sons in your midst, and sons will eat their fathers; and I will carry out judgments upon you and scatter all your remnant to every wind.
native_verses.5:11: Therefore, as I live," declares the Lord GOD, "indeed, because you have defiled My sanctuary with all your loathsome things and with all your abominations, I too will withdraw, and My eye will not look with pity, and I too will have no compassion.
native_verses.5:12: A third of you will die by plague and perish by famine in your midst; a third will fall by the sword all around you; and a third I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.
native_verses.5:13: And My anger will come to an end, and I will let My wrath rest upon them and find relief; and they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in My zeal when I bring My wrath to an end on them.
native_verses.5:14: And I will make you a ruin and a reproach among the nations that are around you, before the eyes of every passerby.
native_verses.5:15: And she will become a reproach and a taunt, an admonition and a horror, to the nations that are around you, when I carry out judgments upon you in anger and in wrath and in rebukes of wrath. I, the LORD, have spoken.
native_verses.5:16: When I send the evil arrows of famine against them, which are for destruction, which I will send to destroy you, then I will increase famine upon you and break for you the staff of bread.
native_verses.5:17: And I will send famine and vicious beasts upon you, and they will bereave you; plague and bloodshed will pass through you, and I will bring a sword upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken."
native_verses.6:1: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.6:2: "Son of man, turn your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them,
native_verses.6:3: and say, 'Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys: "Look, I Myself am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.
native_verses.6:4: And your altars will become desolate, and your incense altars will be shattered, and I will throw down those of you who are killed before your idols.
native_verses.6:5: And I will place the corpses of the sons of Israel in front of their idols, and scatter your bones all around your altars.
native_verses.6:6: In all your dwelling places, the cities will be laid waste and the high places will become desolate, so that your altars will be laid waste and bear guilt, your idols will be shattered and come to an end, your incense altars will be hewn down, and your works will be wiped away.
native_verses.6:7: And those killed will fall in your midst, and you will know that I am the LORD.
native_verses.6:8: Yet I will leave some remaining, in that you will have survivors of the sword among the nations when you are scattered through the lands.
native_verses.6:9: Then your survivors will remember Me among the nations where they were taken captive, how I have been broken by their heart that prostituted itself, which departed from Me, and by their eyes that prostituted themselves after their idols; and they will be disgusted with themselves in their own sight because of the evil things they have done, for all their abominations.
native_verses.6:10: And they will know that I am the LORD; I did not speak in vain about bringing this calamity upon them."'"
native_verses.6:11: This is what the Lord GOD says, "Strike with your hand and stomp with your foot, and say, 'Alas!' over all the wicked abominations of the house of Israel; for by the sword, by famine, and by plague they will fall.
native_verses.6:12: The one who is far away will die by plague, and the one who is near will fall by the sword, and the one who remains and is besieged will die by famine; and I will bring My wrath to an end upon them.
native_verses.6:13: Then you will know that I am the LORD, when those of them who are killed lie in the midst of their idols, all around their altars, on every high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, under every lush tree, and under every thick-branched terebinth, the place where they presented a soothing fragrance to all their idols.
native_verses.6:14: And I will stretch out My hand against them and make the land a desolation and a wasteland, from the wilderness to Diblah, in all their dwelling places; and they will know that I am the LORD."
native_verses.7:1: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.7:2: "And you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says to the soil of Israel: 'An end! The end has come upon the four edges of the land.
native_verses.7:3: Now the end is upon you, and I will send My anger against you, and judge you according to your ways, and lay all your abominations upon you.
native_verses.7:4: And My eye will not spare you, nor will I have compassion; for I will lay your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst; and you will know that I am the LORD.'
native_verses.7:5: This is what the Lord GOD says: 'Disaster, a singular disaster! Look, it is coming!
native_verses.7:6: An end has come; the end has come! It has awakened against you; look, it is coming!
native_verses.7:7: The doom has come to you, inhabitant of the land! The time has come, the day is near—tumult, and not joyful shouting of the mountains.
native_verses.7:8: Now shortly I will pour out My fury upon you, and exhaust My anger against you, and judge you according to your ways, and lay all your abominations upon you.
native_verses.7:9: And My eye will not spare, nor will I have compassion; according to your ways I will repay you, and your abominations will be in your midst; and you will know that I, the LORD, am the one who strikes.
native_verses.7:10: Look, the day! Look, it is coming! The doom has gone out; the rod has bloomed, arrogance has sprouted.
native_verses.7:11: Violence has risen up into a rod of wickedness; none of them, none of their multitude, none of their abundance, nor any eminence among them.
native_verses.7:12: The time has come, the day has arrived; let the buyer not rejoice, and let the seller not mourn, for burning anger is upon all her multitude.
native_verses.7:13: For the seller will not return to what was sold, even while their life is still among the living; for the vision against all her multitude will not turn back, and in his iniquity none of them will sustain his life.
native_verses.7:14: They have sounded the horn and prepared everything, yet no one is going to the battle, for My burning anger is upon all her multitude.
native_verses.7:15: The sword is outside, and the plague and the famine are inside; the one who is in the field will die by the sword, and the one who is in the city—famine and plague will devour him.
native_verses.7:16: And their survivors will escape and be upon the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them groaning, each man because of his iniquity.
native_verses.7:17: All hands will go limp, and all knees will run with water.
native_verses.7:18: And they will wrap themselves in sackcloth, and shuddering will cover them; on every face will be shame, and on all their heads baldness.
native_verses.7:19: They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will become an impure thing; their silver and their gold will not be able to rescue them on the day of the wrath of the LORD. They will not satisfy their appetite, nor will they fill their stomachs, for it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity.
native_verses.7:20: And as for the beauty of its ornament, they turned it into pride, and the images of their abominations—their detestable things—they made with it; therefore I have made it an impure thing to them.
native_verses.7:21: And I will give it into the hand of the foreigners for plunder, and to the wicked of the earth for spoil, and they will profane it.
native_verses.7:22: And I will turn My face away from them, and they will profane My hidden place; and violent men will come into it and profane it.
native_verses.7:23: Make the chain, for the land is filled with crimes of bloodshed, and the city is filled with violence.
native_verses.7:24: And I will bring the most wicked of nations, and they will take possession of their houses; I will end the pride of the mighty, and their sanctuaries will be profaned.
native_verses.7:25: Anguish has come, and they will seek peace, yet there will be none.
native_verses.7:26: Calamity upon calamity will come, and there will be report upon report; they will seek a vision from a prophet, yet instruction will perish from a priest, and counsel from elders.
native_verses.7:27: The king will mourn, and a prince will clothe himself with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land will shake with terror. According to their way I will deal with them, and by their own judgments I will judge them; and they will know that I am the LORD.'"
native_verses.8:1: Now it happened in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was sitting in my house and the elders of Judah were sitting before me, that the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon me there.
native_verses.8:2: Then I looked, and look, a likeness like the appearance of fire: from the appearance of His waist and downward was fire, and from His waist and upward was like the appearance of radiance, like the sheen of glowing metal.
native_verses.8:3: And He stretched out the form of a hand and took hold of me by a lock of my head; and a spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heavens and brought me to Jerusalem in visions of God, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces toward the north, where the seat of the statue of jealousy was, which provokes to jealousy.
native_verses.8:4: And look, there was the glory of the God of Israel, like the appearance that I had seen in the plain.
native_verses.8:5: Then He said to me, "Son of man, lift your eyes now northward." So I lifted my eyes northward, and look, to the north of the gate of the altar was this statue of jealousy in the entryway.
native_verses.8:6: And He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they are doing—the great abominations that the house of Israel is doing here, so that I should go far away from My sanctuary? Yet again you will see great abominations."
native_verses.8:7: Then He brought me to the entrance of the courtyard; and I looked, and look, there was a hole in the wall.
native_verses.8:8: And He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall now." So I dug through the wall, and look, an entrance!
native_verses.8:9: And He said to me, "Go in and see the evil abominations that they are doing here."
native_verses.8:10: So I went in and looked, and look, every form of creeping creature and detestable beast, and all the idols of the house of Israel, was carved upon the wall all the way around.
native_verses.8:11: And seventy men from the elders of the house of Israel—with Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan standing in their midst—were standing before them, each man with his censer in his hand, and the aroma of the cloud of incense was ascending.
native_verses.8:12: Then He said to me, "Have you seen, son of man, what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each man in the chambers of his carved image? For they say, 'The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.'"
native_verses.8:13: And He said to me, "Yet again you will see great abominations that they are doing."
native_verses.8:14: Then He brought me to the entrance of the gate of the house of the LORD that is toward the north, and look, women were sitting there, weeping for Tammuz.
native_verses.8:15: And He said to me, "Have you seen, son of man? Yet again you will see abominations greater than these."
native_verses.8:16: Then He brought me into the inner courtyard of the house of the LORD; and look, at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men, with their backs toward the temple of the LORD and their faces eastward, and they were bowing down eastward to the sun.
native_verses.8:17: And He said to me, "Have you seen, son of man? Is it too light a thing for the house of Judah to do the abominations that they have done here, that they have filled the land with violence and have provoked Me to anger yet again? And look, they are extending the branch to their nose!
native_verses.8:18: And I too will act in fury; My eye will not spare, nor will I have compassion. And they will cry out in My ears with a loud voice, yet I will not listen to them."
native_verses.9:1: Then He cried out in my ears with a loud voice, saying, "The appointed executioners of the city have drawn near, each man with his weapon of destruction in his hand."
native_verses.9:2: And look, six men were coming from the direction of the upper gate that is turned northward, each man with his smashing weapon in his hand; and one man in their midst was clothed in linen, with a scribe's writing kit at his waist. And they came in and stood beside the altar of bronze.
native_verses.9:3: Now the glory of the God of Israel rose up from above the cherub on which it had been to the threshold of the house; and He called to the man clothed in linen who had the scribe's writing kit at his waist.
native_verses.9:4: And the LORD said to him, "Pass through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men who are sighing and groaning over all the abominations that are being done in its midst."
native_verses.9:5: And to these He said in my hearing, "Pass through the city after him and strike; do not let your eye spare, and do not have compassion.
native_verses.9:6: Kill to destruction old men, young men and virgins, little children and women, but do not come near any man on whom is the mark; and begin from My sanctuary." So they began with the elder men who were in front of the house.
native_verses.9:7: And He said to them, "Defile the house, and fill the courtyards with the dead. Go out!" So they went out and struck throughout the city.
native_verses.9:8: And it happened as they were striking, and I was left behind, that I fell upon my face and cried out and said, "Alas, Lord GOD! Are You destroying all the remnant of Israel as You pour out Your fury upon Jerusalem?"
native_verses.9:9: Then He said to me, "The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is great in the extreme; the land has been filled with bloodshed, and the city is full of injustice; for they have said, 'The LORD has forsaken the land, and the LORD does not see.'
native_verses.9:10: And as for Me too, My eye will not spare, nor will I have compassion; I have laid their way upon their heads."
native_verses.9:11: And look, the man clothed in linen, who had the writing kit at his waist, brought back word, saying, "I have done according to all that You commanded me."
native_verses.10:1: Then I looked, and look, upon the expanse that was over the heads of the cherubim, something like a sapphire stone, like the appearance of the likeness of a throne, was seen above them.
native_verses.10:2: And He spoke to the man clothed in linen and said, "Go in among the wheelwork, underneath the cherub, and fill your cupped hands with coals of fire from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city." So he went in before my eyes.
native_verses.10:3: Now the cherubim were standing on the right side of the house when the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner courtyard.
native_verses.10:4: Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherub to the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the courtyard was full of the radiance of the glory of the LORD.
native_verses.10:5: And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard all the way to the outer courtyard, like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks.
native_verses.10:6: Now it happened, when He commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, "Take fire from among the wheelwork, from among the cherubim," that he went in and stood beside the wheel.
native_verses.10:7: Then the cherub stretched out his hand from among the cherubim toward the fire that was among the cherubim, lifted some up, and placed it into the cupped hands of the one clothed in linen, and he took it and went out.
native_verses.10:8: And there appeared on the cherubim the form of a human hand underneath their wings.
native_verses.10:9: Then I looked, and look, four wheels beside the cherubim—one wheel beside one cherub and another wheel beside another cherub—and the appearance of the wheels was like the gleam of a beryl stone.
native_verses.10:10: As for their appearance, all four of them shared one likeness, as though a wheel were within a wheel.
native_verses.10:11: When they moved, they would move toward any of their four sides; they did not turn as they moved, for to the place where the head faced, they followed after it; they did not turn as they moved.
native_verses.10:12: And their whole body, their backs, their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around—the wheels belonging to all four of them.
native_verses.10:13: As for the wheels, they were called "the wheelwork" in my hearing.
native_verses.10:14: And each one had four faces: the first face was the face of the cherub, the second face was the face of a human being, the third was the face of a lion, and the fourth was the face of an eagle.
native_verses.10:15: Then the cherubim rose up. This was the living creature that I had seen at the Chebar River.
native_verses.10:16: When the cherubim moved, the wheels would move beside them; and when the cherubim lifted up their wings to rise off the earth, the wheels also did not turn away from beside them.
native_verses.10:17: When those stood still, these stood still, and when those rose up, these rose up with them, because the spirit of the living creature was in them.
native_verses.10:18: Then the glory of the LORD went out from over the threshold of the house and stood above the cherubim.
native_verses.10:19: And the cherubim lifted up their wings and rose from the earth before my eyes as they went out, with the wheels alongside them; and they stood at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them from above.
native_verses.10:20: This was the living creature that I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the Chebar River, and I knew that they were cherubim.
native_verses.10:21: Each one had four faces, and each one had four wings, and the likeness of human hands was underneath their wings.
native_verses.10:22: As for the likeness of their faces, they were the very faces that I had seen by the Chebar River—their appearance and themselves. Each one moved straight forward.
native_verses.11:1: Then a spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the house of the LORD, which faces eastward. And look, at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men, and among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, officials of the people.
native_verses.11:2: And He said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who devise iniquity and give wicked counsel in this city,
native_verses.11:3: who say, 'Building houses is not near; it is the pot, and we are the meat.'
native_verses.11:4: Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man!"
native_verses.11:5: Then the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me, and He said to me, "Say, 'This is what the LORD says: So you have spoken, house of Israel, and the things that rise in your spirit—I know them.
native_verses.11:6: You have multiplied those you have killed in this city, and you have filled its streets with the dead.
native_verses.11:7: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: Those you have killed, whom you have laid in its midst—they are the meat, and it is the pot; but you will be brought out from its midst.
native_verses.11:8: You have feared a sword, and a sword I will bring upon you, declares the Lord GOD.
native_verses.11:9: And I will bring you out from its midst, and I will give you into the hand of foreigners, and I will execute judgments against you.
native_verses.11:10: By the sword you will fall; at the border of Israel I will judge you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
native_verses.11:11: It will not be a pot for you, nor will you be meat in its midst; at the border of Israel I will judge you.
native_verses.11:12: And you will know that I am the LORD, for you have not walked in My statutes nor carried out My ordinances, but you have acted according to the ordinances of the nations that are around you.'"
native_verses.11:13: Now it happened, as I was prophesying, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell on my face and cried out with a loud voice and said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Are You making a complete end of the remnant of Israel?"
native_verses.11:14: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.11:15: "Son of man, your brothers, your brothers, the men of your kinship, and all the house of Israel, the whole of it—they are the ones to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, 'Stay far away from the LORD; to us this land has been given as a possession.'
native_verses.11:16: Therefore say, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Though I have sent them far away among the nations and though I have scattered them through the lands, yet I have become a sanctuary for them in small measure in the lands where they have gone.'
native_verses.11:17: Therefore say, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you out of the lands in which you have been scattered, and I will give to you the land of Israel.
native_verses.11:18: And they will come there and remove all its detestable things and all its abominations from it.
native_verses.11:19: I will give to them a single heart, and I will place a new spirit within you; I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give to them a heart of flesh,
native_verses.11:20: so that they may walk in My statutes and observe My ordinances and carry them out; and they will be a people to Me, and I will be God to them.
native_verses.11:21: But as for those whose heart goes after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will bring their way upon their own head, declares the Lord GOD.'"
native_verses.11:22: Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, with the wheels alongside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them from above.
native_verses.11:23: And the glory of the LORD went up from over the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain that is east of the city.
native_verses.11:24: And a spirit lifted me up and brought me to Chaldea, to the exiles, in the vision by the Spirit of God. Then the vision that I had seen went up from me.
native_verses.11:25: Then I spoke to the exiles all the words of the LORD that He had shown me.
native_verses.12:1: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.12:2: "Son of man, you are living in the midst of the house of rebellion, who have eyes to see yet do not see, ears to hear yet do not hear, for they are a house of rebellion.
native_verses.12:3: And you, son of man, make ready for yourself belongings for exile, and go into exile by day before their eyes; you shall go into exile from your place to another place before their eyes. Perhaps they will see, though they are a house of rebellion.
native_verses.12:4: And you shall bring out your belongings like belongings for exile by day before their eyes; and you yourself shall go out in the evening before their eyes, like those who go out into exile.
native_verses.12:5: Before their eyes, dig through the wall for yourself, and bring them out through it.
native_verses.12:6: Before their eyes you shall carry them on your shoulder and bring them out in the dark; you shall cover your face so that you do not see the land, for I have appointed you a sign to the house of Israel."
native_verses.12:7: And I did so, just as I was commanded. I brought out my belongings by day like belongings for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall for myself by hand; in the dark I brought them out and carried them on my shoulder before their eyes.
native_verses.12:8: And the word of the LORD came to me in the morning, saying,
native_verses.12:9: "Son of man, did not the house of Israel, the house of rebellion, say to you, 'What are you doing?'
native_verses.12:10: Say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: This burden is about the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are in their midst.'
native_verses.12:11: Say, 'I am your sign. Just as I have done, so it will be done to them: they will go into exile, into captivity.
native_verses.12:12: And the prince who is in their midst will carry a load on his shoulder in the dark and go out. They will dig through the wall to bring him out through it. He will cover his face so that he himself will not see the land with his eyes.
native_verses.12:13: And I will spread out My net over him, and he will be captured in My snare; I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he will not see it, and there he will die.
native_verses.12:14: And all who are around him, his helpers and all his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.
native_verses.12:15: And they will know that I am the LORD when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them through the lands.
native_verses.12:16: Yet I will spare a small number of men among them from sword, from famine, and from pestilence, so that they may recount all their abominations among the nations where they go; and they will know that I am the LORD.'"
native_verses.12:17: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.12:18: "Son of man, you shall eat your bread with trembling, and you shall drink your water with agitation and with anxiety.
native_verses.12:19: And you shall say to the people of the land, 'This is what the Lord GOD says concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem on the soil of Israel: They will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water with horror, so that her land will be desolated of all its fullness because of the violence of all who live in it.
native_verses.12:20: And the inhabited cities will fall into ruin, and the land will become a desolation; then you will know that I am the LORD.'"
native_verses.12:21: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.12:22: "Son of man, what is this proverb you have on the soil of Israel, saying, 'The days stretch out, and every vision perishes'?
native_verses.12:23: Therefore say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: I will put an end to this proverb, and they will no longer repeat it as a proverb in Israel.' Instead, speak to them, 'The days have drawn near, and the word of every vision.
native_verses.12:24: For there will no longer be any empty vision or flattering divination in the midst of the house of Israel.
native_verses.12:25: For I, the LORD, will speak, and whatever word I speak will be done; it will not be postponed any longer. For in your days, house of rebellion, I will speak a word and do it, declares the Lord GOD.'"
native_verses.12:26: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.12:27: "Son of man, look, the house of Israel is saying, 'The vision that he sees is for many days ahead, and for distant times he is prophesying.'
native_verses.12:28: Therefore say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Not one of My words will be postponed any longer; whatever word I speak will be done, declares the Lord GOD.'"
native_verses.13:1: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.13:2: "Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying, and say to those who are prophets from their own hearts, 'Hear the word of the LORD!
native_verses.13:3: This is what the Lord GOD says: Woe upon the foolish prophets who walk after their own spirit and have seen nothing!
native_verses.13:4: Like foxes in the ruins have your prophets been, Israel.
native_verses.13:5: You did not go up into the breaches, nor did you build up a wall around the house of Israel to stand in the battle on the day of the LORD.
native_verses.13:6: They have seen emptiness and lying divination, those who say, "The LORD declares," when the LORD has not sent them; yet they wait for the word to be confirmed.
native_verses.13:7: Have you not seen an empty vision and spoken a lying divination, saying, "The LORD declares," though I have not spoken?
native_verses.13:8: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have spoken emptiness and seen lies, therefore, look, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD.
native_verses.13:9: And My hand will be against the prophets who see emptiness and who divine lies. They will not be in the council of My people, nor will they be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor will they come to the soil of Israel; and you will know that I am the Lord GOD.
native_verses.13:10: Because, yes, because they have misled My people, saying, "Peace," when there is no peace, and when one builds a flimsy wall, look, they plaster it with whitewash.'
native_verses.13:11: Say to those who plaster with whitewash that it will fall: 'A flooding rain will come, and you, hailstones, will fall, and a stormy wind will break out.
native_verses.13:12: And look, the wall has fallen! Will it not be said to you, "Where is the plaster with which you plastered it?"
native_verses.13:13: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: I will cause a stormy wind to break out in My fury, and a flooding rain will come in My anger, and hailstones in fury for complete destruction.
native_verses.13:14: And I will demolish the wall that you plastered with whitewash and bring it down to the ground, and its foundation will be uncovered. And it will fall, and you will be consumed in its midst; and you will know that I am the LORD.
native_verses.13:15: And I will exhaust My fury against the wall and against those who plastered it with whitewash, and I will say to you, "The wall is no more, nor are those who plastered it—
native_verses.13:16: the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and who see for her a vision of peace when there is no peace," declares the Lord GOD.'
native_verses.13:17: As for you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own hearts, and prophesy against them.
native_verses.13:18: And say, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the women who sew bands onto all wrists and make veils for the head of every stature to hunt souls! Will you hunt the souls of My people, and keep souls alive for yourselves?
native_verses.13:19: And you have profaned Me before My people for handfuls of barley and for morsels of bread, to put to death souls that ought not to die and to keep alive souls that ought not to live, by telling lies to My people, who listen to lies.
native_verses.13:20: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I am against your bands with which you hunt souls like birds; I will tear them off your arms, and I will set free the souls that you are hunting, even those souls, like birds.
native_verses.13:21: And I will tear away your veils and rescue My people from your hand, and they will no longer be prey in your hand; then you will know that I am the LORD.
native_verses.13:22: Because you have disheartened the heart of the righteous with falsehood, though I Myself had not caused him pain, and have strengthened the hands of the wicked so that he would not turn back from his evil way to preserve his life,
native_verses.13:23: therefore, you will not see emptiness, nor will you practice divination any longer; and I will rescue My people from your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"
native_verses.14:1: Now men from among the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.
native_verses.14:2: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.14:3: "Son of man, these men have brought up their idols upon their heart and have placed the stumbling block of their iniquity directly in front of their faces. Should I truly allow Myself to be inquired of by them?
native_verses.14:4: Therefore speak with them and say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Any man from the house of Israel who brings up his idols into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity directly in front of his face, and comes to the prophet, I, the LORD, will respond to him who comes with the abundance of his idols,
native_verses.14:5: in order to seize the house of Israel in their heart, because all of them have become estranged from Me through their idols.'
native_verses.14:6: Therefore say to the house of Israel, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Turn back and turn away from your idols, and from all your abominations turn your faces away.
native_verses.14:7: For any man from the house of Israel, or from the sojourner who resides in Israel, who separates himself from following Me and brings up his idols into his heart, and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity directly in front of his face, and comes to the prophet to inquire of Me for himself, I, the LORD, will respond to him by Myself.
native_verses.14:8: And I will set My face against that man and turn him into a sign and bywords, and cut him off from the midst of My people; then you will know that I am the LORD.
native_verses.14:9: And as for the prophet, if he is enticed and speaks a word, I, the LORD, have enticed that prophet; and I will stretch out My hand against him and destroy him from the midst of My people Israel.
native_verses.14:10: And they will bear their iniquity; as the iniquity of the inquirer is, so will the iniquity of the prophet be,
native_verses.14:11: so that the house of Israel may not wander astray from following Me anymore, nor defile themselves anymore with all their transgressions, but may be My people, and I may be their God, declares the Lord GOD.'"
native_verses.14:12: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.14:13: "Son of man, when a land sins against Me by committing treachery, and I stretch out My hand against it, and break its staff of bread, and send famine into it, and cut off from it man and beast,
native_verses.14:14: even if these three men—Noah, Daniel, and Job—were in its midst, they by their righteousness would rescue their own lives, declares the Lord GOD.
native_verses.14:15: If I cause vicious beasts to pass through the land and they bereave it, so that it becomes a desolation with no one passing through because of the beasts,
native_verses.14:16: though these three men were in its midst, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would rescue neither sons nor daughters; they alone would be rescued, while the land would become a desolation.
native_verses.14:17: Or if I bring a sword upon that land and say, 'Let a sword pass through the land,' and I cut off from it man and beast,
native_verses.14:18: even though these three men were in its midst, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would not rescue sons or daughters, but they alone would be rescued.
native_verses.14:19: Or if I send pestilence to that land and pour out My fury on it in blood, in order to cut off from it man and beast,
native_verses.14:20: even though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in its midst, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they would rescue neither son nor daughter; they by their righteousness would rescue their own lives.
native_verses.14:21: For this is what the Lord GOD says: How much more when I send My four disastrous judgments—sword, famine, vicious beasts, and pestilence—against Jerusalem, to cut off from it man and beast!
native_verses.14:22: Yet now, survivors will be left in it who will be brought out, sons and daughters; look, they are coming out to you, and you will see their way and their deeds, and you will be consoled over the disaster that I have brought upon Jerusalem—all that I have brought upon it.
native_verses.14:23: And they will console you when you see their way and their deeds; and you will know that not without reason have I done all that I have done in it, declares the Lord GOD."
native_verses.15:1: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.15:2: "Son of man, how is the wood of the vine superior to any other wood—the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?
native_verses.15:3: Is wood taken from it to be used for any work? Or do people take a peg from it on which to hang any vessel?
native_verses.15:4: Look, it has been given to the fire to be consumed; the fire has consumed both of its ends, and its middle is charred. Is it fit for any work?
native_verses.15:5: Look, while it was whole, it could not be used for any work; how much less, when fire has consumed it and it has been charred, can it still be used for any work?
native_verses.15:6: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Just as the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire to be consumed, so I have given over the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
native_verses.15:7: And I will set My face against them; from the fire they have come out, yet the fire will consume them, and you will know that I am the LORD when I set My face against them.
native_verses.15:8: And I will make the land a desolation, because they have committed treachery, declares the Lord GOD."
